title.zh: 卷四十三 列傳第三 徐羨之 傅亮 檀道濟
title.en: Volume 43 Biographies 3: Xu Xianzhi, Fu Liang, Tan Daoji
title.raw: 卷四十三 列傳第三 徐羨之 傅亮 檀道濟 Volume 43 Biographies 3: Xu Xianzhi, Fu Liang, Tan Daoji

sentences.zh: 列傳第三 徐羨之 傅亮 檀道濟

translations.literal: Biographies 3: Xu Xianzhi, Fu Liang, Tan Daoji
translations.idiomatic: Biographies 3: Xu Xianzhi, Fu Liang, and Tan Daoji

sentences.zh: 徐羨之，字宗文，東海郯人也。

translations.literal: Xu Xianzhi, styled Zongwen, was a man of Tan in Donghai.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Xianzhi, whose style was Zongwen, came from Tan in Donghai commandery.

sentences.zh: 祖寧，尚書吏部郎，江州刺史，未拜卒。

translations.literal: His grandfather Ning was Director of the Secretariat's Personnel Section and Inspector of Jiang Province; he died before assuming the latter post.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Ning had served as director of the Secretariat's personnel section and been appointed inspector of Jiang Province, but died before he could take up that office.

sentences.zh: 父祚之，上虞令。

translations.literal: His father Zuozhi was magistrate of Shangyu.
translations.idiomatic: His father Zuozhi had been magistrate of Shangyu.

sentences.zh: 羨之少為王雅太子少傅主簿，劉牢之鎮北功曹，尚書祠部郎，不拜，桓脩撫軍中兵曹參軍。

translations.literal: In his youth Xianzhi was registrar to Wang Ya, Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent; merit-clerk on Liu Laozhi's northern-pacification staff; Director of Sacrifices in the Secretariat, which he declined; and military aide on Huan Xiu's pacification staff.
translations.idiomatic: In his youth Xianzhi served as registrar to the Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent Wang Ya, as merit-clerk on the northern-pacification staff of Liu Laozhi, and as director of sacrifices in the Secretariat—a post he declined—before becoming a military aide on the pacification staff of Huan Xiu.

sentences.zh: 與高祖同府，深相親結。

translations.literal: He was in the same office as Gaozu and they became deeply intimate.
translations.idiomatic: He served in the same office as Gaozu, and the two became close friends.

sentences.zh: 義旗建，高祖版為鎮軍參軍，尚書庫部郎，領軍司馬。

translations.literal: When the righteous banner was raised, Gaozu appointed him Military Staff Officer of the Pacification Army, Director of the Stores Section in the Secretariat, and Marshal of the Palace Guard.
translations.idiomatic: When the righteous army was raised, Gaozu appointed him staff officer of the Pacification Army, director of the stores section in the Secretariat, and marshal of the palace guard.

sentences.zh: 與謝混共事，混甚知之。

translations.literal: He worked together with Xie Hun, who knew him very well.
translations.idiomatic: He worked alongside Xie Hun, who came to know him very well indeed.

sentences.zh: 補琅邪王大司馬參軍，司徒左西屬，徐州別駕從事史，太尉諮議參軍。

translations.literal: He was successively made staff officer to the Grand Marshal, Prince of Langye; western aide to the Minister of Education; aide-de-camp to the governor of Xuzhou; and consulting staff officer to the Grand Commander.
translations.idiomatic: He was then assigned in turn as staff officer to the Grand Marshal, Prince of Langye; as western aide to the Minister of Education; as aide-de-camp to the governor of Xuzhou; and as consulting staff officer to the Grand Commander.

sentences.zh: 義熙十一年，除鷹揚將軍、琅邪內史，仍為大司馬從事中郎，將軍如故。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year of Yixi he was made General Who Stirs the Hawks and Administrator of Langye Interior, and continued as Attendant Gentleman on the Grand Marshal's staff with his generalship unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year of Yixi (415), he was appointed General Who Stirs the Hawks and administrator of Langye Interior, while retaining his post as attendant gentleman on the Grand Marshal's staff with his general's rank unchanged.

sentences.zh: 高祖北伐，轉太尉左司馬，掌留任，以副貳劉穆之。

translations.literal: When Gaozu marched north, he was transferred to Left Marshal of the Grand Commander, placed in charge of duties left behind, to assist Liu Muzhi as deputy.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu launched his northern campaign, Xianzhi was transferred to left marshal of the Grand Commander and put in charge of affairs left behind at the capital, serving as Liu Muzhi's deputy.

sentences.zh: 初，高祖議欲北伐，朝士多諫，唯羨之默然。

translations.literal: At first, when Gaozu debated a northern campaign, many court officials remonstrated; only Xianzhi was silent.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Gaozu first proposed a northern expedition, many officials at court urged him against it; Xianzhi alone said nothing.

sentences.zh: 或問何獨不言，羨之曰：「吾位至二品，官為二千石，志願久充。

translations.literal: Someone asked why he alone did not speak. Xianzhi said: "My rank has reached the second grade and my office is at two thousand dan; my ambitions have long been fulfilled.
translations.idiomatic: When someone asked why he alone had kept silent, Xianzhi replied: "My rank has already reached the second grade and my office carries two thousand dan of salary—my ambitions have long since been satisfied.

sentences.zh: 今二方已平，拓地萬里，唯有小羌未定，而公寢食不忘。

translations.literal: Now the two regions are pacified and territory has been extended ten thousand li; only the petty Qiang remain unsettled, yet my lord cannot eat or sleep without thinking of them.
translations.idiomatic: The two rival states are already pacified and our territory stretches ten thousand li; only the petty Qiang tribes remain unsettled, yet my lord cannot eat or sleep for thinking of them.

sentences.zh: 意量乖殊，何可輕豫。

translations.literal: His intent and scope are utterly unlike mine—how could I lightly presume to intervene?"
translations.idiomatic: His vision and mine are worlds apart—how could I lightly presume to offer advice?"

sentences.zh: 」劉穆之卒，高祖命以羨之為吏部尚書、建威將軍、丹陽尹，總知留任，甲仗二十人出入。

translations.literal: When Liu Muzhi died, Gaozu ordered Xianzhi to be Director of Personnel, General Who Establishes Might, and Governor of Danyang, with overall charge of remaining duties and twenty armed men on his comings and goings.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Muzhi died, Gaozu appointed Xianzhi director of personnel, General Who Establishes Might, and governor of Danyang, with overall charge of affairs at the capital and an escort of twenty armed men whenever he went out.

sentences.zh: 轉尚書僕射，將軍、尹如故。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Vice Director of the Secretariat; his generalship and governorship remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: He was then promoted to vice director of the Secretariat, retaining his general's rank and his post as governor of Danyang.

sentences.zh: 十四年，大司馬府軍人朱興妻周坐息男道扶年三歲，先得癇病，周因其病發，掘地生埋之，為道扶姑女所告，正周棄市刑。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year, Zhou, wife of Zhu Xing, a soldier of the Grand Marshal's command, was charged because her son Daofu, aged three, had earlier contracted epilepsy; when the illness flared Zhou dug a pit and buried him alive; Daofu's paternal aunt's daughter reported it, and Zhou was sentenced to execution and exposure in the marketplace.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year, a soldier of the Grand Marshal's command named Zhu Xing had a wife, Zhou, who was prosecuted because her son Daofu, aged three, had earlier fallen ill with epilepsy; when the seizure came on, Zhou dug a pit and buried the boy alive. Daofu's cousin by marriage reported the crime, and Zhou was sentenced to execution and exposure in the marketplace.

sentences.zh: 羨之議曰：「自然之愛，虎狼猶仁。

translations.literal: Xianzhi submitted an opinion: "Natural affection—even tigers and wolves show kindness.
translations.idiomatic: Xianzhi submitted a memorial arguing: "Natural parental love moves even tigers and wolves to show kindness.

sentences.zh: 周之凶忍，宜加顯戮。

translations.literal: Zhou's cruelty warrants conspicuous execution.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou's savage cruelty plainly warrants the severest punishment.

sentences.zh: 臣以為法律之外，故尚弘物之理。

translations.literal: Your servant believes that beyond the statutes one should still uphold the principle of extending compassion to living things.
translations.idiomatic: Yet beyond the letter of the law, Your Majesty should still uphold the principle of extending compassion to all living beings.

sentences.zh: 母之即刑，由子明法，為子之道，焉有自容之地。

translations.literal: When a mother faces execution because her son has clarified the law, in the way of a son what place remains for self-respect?
translations.idiomatic: When a mother faces execution because her son has exposed her crime, what room can there be for a son to hold his head high?

sentences.zh: 雖伏法者當罪，而在宥者靡容。

translations.literal: Though the one who submits to the law is guilty, the one who is spared has no place to stand.
translations.idiomatic: Though the one who submits to punishment deserves guilt, the one who is spared has nowhere to turn.

sentences.zh: 愚謂可特申之遐裔。

translations.literal: Your servant proposes that he may specially be sent to a distant border region."
translations.idiomatic: I humbly propose that the son be specially banished to a distant frontier region instead."

sentences.zh: 」從之。

translations.literal: The proposal was adopted.
translations.idiomatic: The court accepted his proposal.

sentences.zh: 高祖踐阼，進號鎮軍將軍，加散騎常侍。

translations.literal: When Gaozu ascended the throne, Xianzhi was advanced to General of the Pacification Army and given the additional title of Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu took the throne, Xianzhi was promoted to General of the Pacification Army and given the additional title of regular attendant of the scattered cavalry.

sentences.zh: 上初即位，思佐命之功，詔曰：「散騎常侍、尚書僕射、鎮軍將軍、丹陽尹徐羨之，監江州、豫州之西陽、新蔡諸軍事、撫軍將軍、江州刺史華容侯王弘，散騎常侍、護軍將軍作唐男檀道濟，中書令、領太子詹事傅亮，侍中、中領軍謝晦，前左將軍、江州刺史宜陽侯檀韶，使持節、雍、梁、南、北秦四州、荊州之河北諸軍事、後將軍、雍州刺史關中侯趙倫之，使持節、督北徐、兗、青三州諸軍事、征虜將軍、北徐州刺史南城男劉懷慎，散騎常侍、領太子左衛率新淦侯王仲德，前冠軍將軍、北青州刺史安南男向彌，左衛將軍灄陽男劉粹，使持節、南蠻校尉佷山子到彥之，西中郎司馬南郡宜陽侯張邵，參西中郎將軍事、建威將軍、河東太守資中侯沈林子等，或忠規遠謀，扶贊洪業；

translations.literal: When the emperor first took the throne, mindful of those who had aided his founding mandate, he issued an edict: "Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry, Vice Director of the Secretariat, General of the Pacification Army, and Governor of Danyang Xu Xianzhi; Wang Hong, Marquis of Huarong, General Who Pacifies the Army and Inspector of Jiang Province supervising military affairs in Xiyang and Xincai of Jiang and Yu provinces; Tan Daoji, Baron of Zuotang, Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry and General Who Guards the Army; Fu Liang, Director of the Secretariat and Concurrent Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent; Xie Hui, Palace Attendant and Central Commander of the Palace Guard; Tan Shao, former General of the Left and Inspector of Jiang Province, Marquis of Yiyang; Zhao Lunzhi, Marquis of Guanzhong, bearer of the staff of authority, Rear General and Inspector of Yong Province supervising military affairs in Yong, Liang, and the four Qin provinces and the north bank of Jing Province; Liu Huaishen, Baron of Nancheng, bearer of the staff of authority, General Who Punishes the Barbarians and Inspector of Northern Xuzhou supervising military affairs in Northern Xu, Yan, and Qing provinces; Wang Zhongde, Marquis of Xingan, Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry and Commander of the Left Guards of the Heir Apparent; Xiang Mi, former General Who Conquers the Champions and Inspector of Northern Qing Province, Baron of Annan; Liu Cui, Baron of Shanyang, General of the Left Guards; Dao Yanzhi, Son of Gen Mountain, bearer of the staff of authority and Colonel of the Southern Man; Zhang Shao, Marquis of Yiyang of Nan commandery, Marshal of the Western Palace Gentleman; Shen Linzi, Marquis of Zizhong, staff officer on the Western Palace Gentleman's campaign, General Who Establishes Might, and Administrator of Hedong—some with loyal counsel and far-reaching plans who upheld the great enterprise;
translations.idiomatic: Soon after his accession, mindful of those who had helped him win the throne, the emperor issued an edict: "Xu Xianzhi, regular attendant of the scattered cavalry, vice director of the Secretariat, general of the pacification army, and governor of Danyang; Wang Hong, Marquis of Huarong, general who pacifies the army and inspector of Jiang Province; Tan Daoji, Baron of Zuotang, regular attendant of the scattered cavalry and general who guards the army; Fu Liang, director of the Secretariat and concurrent grand tutor of the heir apparent; Xie Hui, palace attendant and central commander of the palace guard; Tan Shao, former general of the left and inspector of Jiang Province, Marquis of Yiyang; Zhao Lunzhi, Marquis of Guanzhong, rear general and inspector of Yong Province; Liu Huaishen, Baron of Nancheng, general who punishes the barbarians and inspector of Northern Xuzhou; Wang Zhongde, Marquis of Xingan, regular attendant of the scattered cavalry and commander of the left guards of the heir apparent; Xiang Mi, former general who conquers the champions and inspector of Northern Qing Province, Baron of Annan; Liu Cui, Baron of Shanyang, general of the left guards; Dao Yanzhi, Son of Gen Mountain, colonel of the southern barbarians; Zhang Shao, Marquis of Yiyang of Nan commandery, marshal of the western palace gentleman; Shen Linzi, Marquis of Zizhong, general who establishes might and administrator of Hedong—some offered loyal counsel and far-sighted plans that upheld the great enterprise;

sentences.zh: 或肆勤樹績，弘濟艱難。

translations.literal: some exerted diligence and built merit, broadly relieving hardship.
translations.idiomatic: others labored tirelessly and built up achievements that eased the empire through its hardest trials.

sentences.zh: 經始圖終，勳烈惟茂，並宜與國同休，饗茲大賚。

translations.literal: From beginning to end they planned and completed; their merit and glory are especially abundant—all should share the state's good fortune and enjoy this great reward.
translations.idiomatic: From the founding through to its completion, their merit has been outstanding, and all alike should share the state's good fortune and receive this great reward.

sentences.zh: 羨之可封南昌縣公，弘可華容縣公，道濟可改封永脩縣公，亮可建城縣公，晦可武昌縣公，食邑各二千戶；

translations.literal: Xianzhi may be enfeoffed as Duke of Nanchang county; Hong as Duke of Huarong county; Daoji may have his fief changed to Duke of Yongxiu county; Liang as Duke of Jiancheng county; Hui as Duke of Wuchang county—each with a fief of two thousand households;
translations.idiomatic: Xianzhi shall be enfeoffed as Duke of Nanchang with a fief of two thousand households; Hong as Duke of Huarong; Daoji's fief shall be changed to Duke of Yongxiu; Liang as Duke of Jiancheng; and Hui as Duke of Wuchang—each with two thousand households;

sentences.zh: 韶可更增邑二千五百戶，仲德可增邑二千二百戶；

translations.literal: Shao may have his fief further increased by two thousand five hundred households; Zhongde by two thousand two hundred households;
translations.idiomatic: Shao's fief shall be further increased by two thousand five hundred households, and Zhongde's by two thousand two hundred;

sentences.zh: 懷慎、彥之各進爵為侯，粹改封建安縣侯，並增邑為千戶；

translations.literal: Huaishen and Yanzhi shall each be advanced to marquis; Cui's fief shall be changed to Marquis of Jian'an county, each with fiefs increased to one thousand households;
translations.idiomatic: Huaishen and Yanzhi shall each be advanced to marquis; Cui's title shall be changed to Marquis of Jian'an, each with a fief of one thousand households;

sentences.zh: 倫之可封霄城縣侯，食邑千戶；

translations.literal: Lunzhi may be enfeoffed as Marquis of Xiaocheng county with a fief of one thousand households;
translations.idiomatic: Lunzhi shall be enfeoffed as Marquis of Xiaocheng with a fief of one thousand households;

sentences.zh: 邵可封臨沮縣伯，林子可封漢壽縣伯，食邑六百戶。

translations.literal: Shao may be enfeoffed as Baron of Linju county; Linzi as Baron of Hanshou county—each with a fief of six hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: Shao shall be enfeoffed as Baron of Linju and Linzi as Baron of Hanshou, each with a fief of six hundred households.

sentences.zh: 開國之制，率遵舊章。」

translations.literal: The regulations for establishing a state shall in all cases follow the former statutes."
translations.idiomatic: The regulations governing the establishment of noble estates shall in all cases follow the former statutes."

sentences.zh: 羨之遷尚書令、揚州刺史，加散騎常侍。

translations.literal: Xianzhi was transferred to Director of the Secretariat and Inspector of Yang Province, with the additional title of Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: Xianzhi was promoted to director of the Secretariat and inspector of Yang Province, with the additional title of regular attendant of the scattered cavalry.

sentences.zh: 進位司空、錄尚書事，常侍、刺史如故。

translations.literal: He was advanced to Minister of Works and Recorder of Affairs of the Secretariat; his attendant and inspector posts remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: He was further promoted to minister of works and recorder of Secretariat affairs, retaining his posts as attendant and inspector.

sentences.zh: 羨之起布衣，又無術學，直以志力局度，一旦居廊廟，朝野推服，咸謂有宰臣之望。

translations.literal: Xianzhi rose from commoner status and had no scholarly training; relying solely on will, strength, and breadth of vision, he suddenly occupied the highest offices, and court and countryside alike deferred to him, all saying he had the makings of a chief minister.
translations.idiomatic: Xianzhi had risen from commoner origins without scholarly training, yet through force of will and breadth of vision he suddenly found himself at the summit of government; court and country alike deferred to him, and all agreed he had the makings of a chief minister.

sentences.zh: 沈密寡言，不以憂喜見色。

translations.literal: He was deep and secretive, sparing of speech, and did not show joy or sorrow in his expression.
translations.idiomatic: Deep and reserved, he spoke little and never let joy or sorrow show on his face.

sentences.zh: 頗工弈棊，觀戲常若未解，當世倍以此推之。

translations.literal: He was quite skilled at weiqi; when watching games he often seemed not to understand them, and his contemporaries doubly admired him for this.
translations.idiomatic: He was quite skilled at weiqi, yet when watching others play he often seemed not to understand the game at all—an affectation his contemporaries admired all the more for the restraint it implied.

sentences.zh: 傅亮、蔡廓常言：「徐公曉萬事，安異同。」

translations.literal: Fu Liang and Cai Kuo often said: "Lord Xu understands all affairs and settles differences and agreements."
translations.idiomatic: Fu Liang and Cai Kuo were fond of saying: "Lord Xu understands everything and knows how to reconcile opposing views."

sentences.zh: 高祖不豫，加班劍三十人。

translations.literal: When Gaozu fell ill, thirty armed attendants were added to Xianzhi's escort.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu fell gravely ill, thirty armed attendants were added to Xianzhi's escort.

sentences.zh: 宮車晏駕，與中書令傅亮、領軍將軍謝晦、鎮北將軍檀道濟同被顧命。

translations.literal: When the imperial carriage halted at dusk, he was together with Director of the Secretariat Fu Liang, General Who Commands the Army Xie Hui, and General Who Pacifies the North Tan Daoji entrusted with the final mandate.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor died, Xianzhi was named, together with Fu Liang, director of the Secretariat; Xie Hui, general who commands the army; and Tan Daoji, general who pacifies the north, among those entrusted with the dying emperor's final mandate.

sentences.zh: 少帝詔曰：「平理獄訟，政道所先。

translations.literal: The Young Emperor issued an edict: "Settling lawsuits is what government should put first.
translations.idiomatic: The Young Emperor issued an edict: "The fair resolution of lawsuits is the foremost duty of government.

sentences.zh: 朕哀荒在疚，未堪親覽。

translations.literal: I am in the depths of mourning and not yet able to review cases personally.
translations.idiomatic: I am still deep in mourning and not yet able to review cases in person.

sentences.zh: 司空、尚書令可率眾官月一決獄。」

translations.literal: The Minister of Works and Director of the Secretariat may lead all officials in holding court once a month to decide cases."
translations.idiomatic: The minister of works and director of the Secretariat shall lead the officials in holding court once a month to decide cases."

sentences.zh: 帝後失德，羨之等將謀廢立，而廬陵王義真輕動多過，不任四海，乃先廢義真，然後廢帝。

translations.literal: The emperor later lost virtue; Xianzhi and the others planned to depose and replace him, but Prince of Luling Yizhen was rash and full of faults and unfit to rule the realm, so they first deposed Yizhen and only then deposed the emperor.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor soon proved unfit to rule, and Xianzhi and his colleagues resolved to depose him. But Prince of Luling Yizhen was rash and error-prone and unfit to receive the realm, so they deposed Yizhen first and only then moved against the emperor himself.

sentences.zh: 時謝晦為領軍，以府舍內屋敗應治，悉移家人出宅，聚將士於府內。

translations.literal: At that time Xie Hui was commander of the army; citing dilapidated buildings within his headquarters that needed repair, he moved all his family out of the residence and gathered troops inside.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Xie Hui held command of the palace guard. Citing dilapidated buildings within his headquarters that required repair, he moved his entire household out of the residence and gathered his troops inside.

sentences.zh: 鎮北將軍、南兗州刺史檀道濟先朝舊將，威服殿省，且有兵眾，召使入朝，告之以謀。

translations.literal: Tan Daoji, General Who Pacifies the North and Inspector of Southern Yanzhou, was an old general of the previous reign who awed the palace offices and had troops; they summoned him to court and informed him of the plot.
translations.idiomatic: Tan Daoji, general who pacifies the north and inspector of Southern Yanzhou, was a veteran general of the previous reign whose authority awed the palace offices and who commanded substantial forces; they summoned him to court and disclosed the plot.

sentences.zh: 事將發，道濟入宿領軍府。

translations.literal: As the affair was about to unfold, Daoji entered and lodged at the commander's headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: On the eve of the coup, Daoji took up quarters inside the commander's headquarters.

sentences.zh: 中書舍人邢安泰、潘盛為內應，其日守關。

translations.literal: Palace Secretariat attendants Xing Antai and Pan Sheng served as insiders; that day they guarded the gates.
translations.idiomatic: Palace attendants Xing Antai and Pan Sheng served as insiders, and on the appointed day they held the palace gates.

sentences.zh: 道濟領兵居前，羨之等繼其後，由東掖門、雲龍門入，宿衛先受處分，莫有動者。

translations.literal: Daoji led troops in front while Xianzhi and the others followed; they entered through the Eastern Side Gate and Cloud Dragon Gate; the palace guards had already received their orders and none stirred.
translations.idiomatic: Daoji led the troops in the van while Xianzhi and the others followed behind; they entered through the Eastern Side Gate and the Cloud Dragon Gate. The palace guards had already been given their orders, and not one moved.

sentences.zh: 先是帝於華林園為列肆，親自酤賣，又開瀆聚土，以象破崗，率左右唱呼引船為樂。

translations.literal: Earlier the emperor had set up rows of shops in Hualin Garden and sold wine himself; he also dug a channel and piled earth to imitate Broken Hill, leading his attendants in chanting and hauling boats for amusement.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier that day the emperor had set up market stalls in Hualin Garden and sold wine himself; he had also dug a channel and piled up earth to imitate Broken Hill, leading his attendants in chants as they hauled boats about for amusement.

sentences.zh: 是夕，寢於龍舟，在天淵池。

translations.literal: That evening he slept on the dragon boat in the Celestial Pool.
translations.idiomatic: That evening he was asleep aboard the dragon boat on the Celestial Pool.

sentences.zh: 兵士進殺二人，又傷帝指。

translations.literal: Soldiers advanced and killed two men, and also wounded the emperor's finger.
translations.idiomatic: Soldiers advanced and killed two of his attendants, wounding the emperor's finger in the process.

sentences.zh: 扶帝出東閣，收璽綬。

translations.literal: They supported the emperor out through the eastern pavilion and seized the seals and cords.
translations.idiomatic: They helped the emperor out through the eastern pavilion and seized the imperial seals and regalia.

sentences.zh: 群臣拜辭，衛送故太子宮，遷於吳郡。

translations.literal: The officials bowed in farewell; guards escorted him to the former heir apparent's palace and he was transferred to Wu commandery.
translations.idiomatic: The officials bowed in farewell; guards escorted him to the former heir apparent's residence, and he was then transferred to Wu commandery.

sentences.zh: 侍中程道惠勸立第五皇弟義恭，羨之不許。

translations.literal: Palace Attendant Cheng Daohui urged that the fifth imperial younger brother Yigong be enthroned; Xianzhi would not agree.
translations.idiomatic: Palace attendant Cheng Daohui urged that the fifth imperial brother, Yigong, be enthroned instead, but Xianzhi refused.

sentences.zh: 遣使殺義真於新安，殺帝於吳縣。

translations.literal: They sent envoys to kill Yizhen at Xin'an and the emperor at Wu county.
translations.idiomatic: They dispatched envoys to kill Yizhen at Xin'an and the deposed emperor at Wu county.

sentences.zh: 時為帝築宮未成，權居金昌亭，帝突走出昌門，追者以門關擊之倒地，然後加害。

translations.literal: At that time the palace being built for the emperor was not yet finished; he was lodged provisionally at Jinchang Pavilion; the emperor suddenly ran out through Chang Gate; pursuers struck him down with the gate bar and then killed him.
translations.idiomatic: A residence was still under construction for the deposed emperor, so he was lodged temporarily at Jinchang Pavilion. He suddenly bolted out through Chang Gate; his pursuers struck him down with the gate bar and only then delivered the fatal blow.

sentences.zh: 太祖即阼，進羨之司徒，餘如故，改封南平郡公，食邑四千戶，固讓加封。

translations.literal: When Taizu ascended the throne, Xianzhi was advanced to Minister of Education with other posts unchanged; his fief was changed to Duke of Nanping commandery with four thousand households; he firmly declined the added enfeoffment.
translations.idiomatic: When Taizu took the throne, Xianzhi was promoted to minister of education with his other posts unchanged; his title was changed to Duke of Nanping commandery with a fief of four thousand households, though he firmly declined the added enfeoffment.

sentences.zh: 有司奏車駕依舊臨華林園聽訟，詔曰：「政刑多所未悉，可如先二公推訊。」

translations.literal: The relevant offices memorialized that the imperial carriage should as before attend at Hualin Garden to hear cases; an edict said: "Government and punishments are largely still unfamiliar—proceed as the two former lords conducted inquiries."
translations.idiomatic: The relevant offices proposed that the emperor should as before attend at Hualin Garden to hear lawsuits in person. An edict replied: "I am still largely unfamiliar with government and the administration of justice—let matters proceed as the two former chief ministers conducted their inquiries."

sentences.zh: 元嘉二年，羨之與左光祿大夫傅亮上表歸政，曰：「臣聞元首司契，運樞成務；

translations.literal: In the second year of Yuanjia, Xianzhi and Left Grand Master of the Palace Fu Liang submitted a memorial returning power, saying: "Your servants have heard that the sovereign holds the tally and turns the pivot to accomplish the tasks;
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Yuanjia, Xianzhi and the left grand master of the palace Fu Liang submitted a memorial offering to return power to the throne, stating: "We have heard that the sovereign holds the mandate of heaven and turns the pivot of state to accomplish the great tasks of government;

sentences.zh: 臣道代終，事盡宣翼。

translations.literal: the way of subjects ends with their generation and their affairs reach only to assisting and supporting.
translations.idiomatic: the way of subjects ends with their own generation, and their duty extends no further than to assist and support.

sentences.zh: 冕旒之道，理絕於上皇；

translations.literal: The way of the imperial cap-strings is logically cut off from the highest sovereign;
translations.idiomatic: The way of the imperial regalia belongs solely to the supreme sovereign;

sentences.zh: 拱己之事，不行於中古。

translations.literal: the practice of folding one's arms and leaving affairs alone was not practiced in the middle antiquity.
translations.idiomatic: and the practice of folding one's arms and leaving affairs to others was unknown even in middle antiquity.

sentences.zh: 故高宗不言，以三齡為斷；

translations.literal: Therefore Gaozong of the Shang did not speak, taking three years as the limit;
translations.idiomatic: Thus Gaozong of the Shang did not speak aloud for three years;

sentences.zh: 塚宰聽政，以再期為節。

translations.literal: the chief minister heard government for two years as the term.
translations.idiomatic: and the chief minister governed in his stead for two years as the established term.

sentences.zh: 百王以降，罔或不然。

translations.literal: From the hundred kings downward, none have been otherwise.
translations.idiomatic: From the hundred kings of antiquity down to the present, none have been otherwise.

sentences.zh: 陛下聖德紹興，負荷洪業，億兆顒顒，思陶盛化。

translations.literal: Your Majesty's sagely virtue continues the rise; you bear the great enterprise; the hundred millions look up eagerly, thinking to be molded by flourishing transformation.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty's sagely virtue continues the dynasty's rise; you bear the great enterprise upon your shoulders; the hundred millions look up eagerly, longing to be shaped by your flourishing rule.

sentences.zh: 而聖旨謙挹，委成群司。

translations.literal: Yet the sacred intent is humble and restrained, entrusting affairs to the assembled offices.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Your Majesty's sacred intent remains humble and restrained, entrusting affairs to your assembled ministers.

sentences.zh: 自大禮告終，鑽燧三改，大明佇照，遠邇傾屬。

translations.literal: Since the great rites were concluded, the fire-drill and flint have changed three times; the great brightness waits to shine forth, and far and near lean toward it.
translations.idiomatic: Since the great mourning rites concluded, three seasons have passed; the great brightness waits to shine forth, and far and near alike turn toward it.

sentences.zh: 臣等雖率誠屢聞，未能仰感，敢藉品物之情，謹因蒼生之志。

translations.literal: Your servants, though repeatedly offering our sincerity, have been unable to move Your Majesty upward; we venture to borrow the feelings of all things and respectfully follow the will of the black-haired people.
translations.idiomatic: We your servants have repeatedly offered our sincere counsel yet have been unable to move Your Majesty; we venture now to speak on behalf of all living things and in accordance with the will of the people.

sentences.zh: 伏願陛下遠存周文日昃之道，近思皇室締構之艱，時攬萬機，躬親朝政，廣辟四聰，博詢庶業，則雍熙可臻，有生幸甚。

translations.literal: We prostrate ourselves in wishing that Your Majesty will far preserve the way of King Wen of Zhou, who worked until sunset; near recall the hardships of the imperial house's founding; from time to time grasp the myriad affairs and personally attend to court government; broadly open the four keen ears and widely inquire into all occupations—then harmonious splendor may be reached and all who live will be greatly fortunate.
translations.idiomatic: We humbly pray that Your Majesty will look back to King Wen of Zhou, who labored until sunset, and recall the hardships of our own dynasty's founding; that you will from time to time take up the myriad affairs of state and attend to government in person; that you will open wide the four avenues of counsel and inquire broadly into all matters of governance—then harmonious prosperity may be achieved, to the great fortune of all who live under heaven.

sentences.zh: 」上未許。

translations.literal: The emperor did not consent.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor did not consent.

sentences.zh: 羨之等重奏曰：「近寫下情，言為心罄，奉被還詔，鑒許未回。

translations.literal: Xianzhi and the others submitted again: "Recently we set down our feelings below; our words came from the exhaustion of our hearts; we received the returned edict, but approval and consent have not turned back.
translations.idiomatic: Xianzhi and his colleagues submitted again: "We recently set down our deepest feelings; our words came straight from the heart. We received Your Majesty's reply, yet approval has not been granted.

sentences.zh: 豈惟愚臣秉心有在，詢之朝野，人無異議。

translations.literal: Is it only that your foolish servants hold their hearts firm? Inquiring of court and countryside, no one has a differing opinion.
translations.idiomatic: Is it only we foolish ministers who hold this conviction? Ask anyone at court or in the countryside—there is not a dissenting voice.

sentences.zh: 何者？

translations.literal: Why?
translations.idiomatic: Why is this so?

sentences.zh: 形風四方，實繫王德，一國之事，本之一人。

translations.literal: The formative influence over the four directions truly depends on the king's virtue; the affairs of a state root in one person.
translations.idiomatic: The moral influence that shapes the four directions truly depends on the sovereign's virtue; the affairs of an entire state root in a single person.

sentences.zh: 雖世代不同，時殊風異，至於主運臣贊，古今一揆。

translations.literal: Though generations differ and times and customs vary, as for the sovereign's movement and the subjects' support, ancient and modern are one standard.
translations.idiomatic: Though generations differ and times and customs vary, the relationship between sovereign and subject has always been the same.

sentences.zh: 未有渾心委任，而休明可期，此之非宜，布自遐邇。

translations.literal: Never has there been one who with a muddled heart entrusted affairs to others yet could expect enlightened splendor—this impropriety is known from far to near.
translations.idiomatic: Never yet has a ruler who entrusted his heart and affairs entirely to others been able to expect an age of enlightened splendor—this impropriety is understood from the farthest reaches to the nearest.

sentences.zh: 臣等荷遇二世，休戚以均，情為國至，豈容順默。

translations.literal: Your servants have received favor from two reigns and share joy and sorrow equally; our feeling reaches to the state—how could we comply in silence?
translations.idiomatic: We have received favor from two reigns and share equally in the dynasty's joys and sorrows; our devotion to the state runs to the utmost—how could we comply in silence?

sentences.zh: 重披丹心，冒昧以請。

translations.literal: Again laying bare our red hearts, we venture impertinently to request.
translations.idiomatic: We lay bare our hearts once more and venture, impertinently, to ask again.

sentences.zh: 」上猶辭。

translations.literal: The emperor still declined.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor still declined.

sentences.zh: 羨之等又固陳曰：「比表披陳，辭誠俱盡，詔旨沖遠，未垂聽納，三復屏營，伏增憂歎。

translations.literal: Xianzhi and the others again firmly submitted: "Recently in our memorial we laid everything bare; our words and sincerity were fully spent; the edict's intent is lofty and distant and has not yet granted acceptance; thrice reviewing it we are anxious and uneasy, prostrate and increased in worry and sighs.
translations.idiomatic: Xianzhi and his colleagues submitted yet again: "In our recent memorial we laid everything bare and spoke with complete sincerity; yet Your Majesty's lofty reply has not granted acceptance. Having read it three times over, we are filled with anxiety and dread, and our worry only deepens.

sentences.zh: 臣聞克隆先構，幹蠱之盛業；

translations.literal: Your servants have heard that continuing and enlarging the prior structure is the great enterprise of carrying on the founding;
translations.idiomatic: We have heard that continuing and enlarging the work of one's predecessors is the great enterprise of a dynasty;

sentences.zh: 昧旦丕顯，帝王之高義。

translations.literal: working from before dawn to grandly display is the lofty righteousness of emperors and kings.
translations.idiomatic: and that laboring from before dawn to bring glory to the realm is the highest duty of every emperor and king.

sentences.zh: 自皇宋創運，英聖有造，殷憂未闕，艱患仍纏。

translations.literal: Since the Song dynasty was founded, heroic sages have created it; deep sorrow has not ceased and hard calamities still entwine.
translations.idiomatic: Since the Song dynasty was founded, heroic and sage rulers have built it up, yet deep sorrows have not ceased and hard trials still entwine the realm.

sentences.zh: 賴天命有底，聖明承業，時屯國故，猶在民心。

translations.literal: Relying on Heaven's mandate having a foundation, sagely brightness inherits the enterprise; though the time is troubled and state affairs are difficult, they still rest in the people's hearts.
translations.idiomatic: Thanks to Heaven's mandate having a firm foundation, a sage ruler now inherits the enterprise; though the times are troubled and state affairs remain difficult, the people's hearts still rest in the throne.

sentences.zh: 泰山之安，未易可保，昏明隆替，繫在聖躬。

translations.literal: The security of Mount Tai is not easily preserved; the rise and fall of darkness and brightness depend on the sacred person.
translations.idiomatic: The security of Mount Tai is not easily preserved; whether the age grows dark or bright depends on Your Majesty's own person.

sentences.zh: 斯誠周詩夙興之辰，殷王待旦之日，豈得無為拱己，復玄古之風，逡巡虛挹，徇匹夫之事。

translations.literal: This is truly the hour of early rising in the Zhou odes, the day of the Shang king waiting for dawn—how can one be inactive, fold one's arms, restore the wind of deepest antiquity, hesitate and emptyly yield, and follow the affairs of a common man?
translations.idiomatic: This is truly the hour of early rising praised in the Zhou odes, the day of the Shang king waiting for dawn—how can Your Majesty remain inactive, fold your arms, and seek to restore the ways of deepest antiquity, hesitating and yielding power while attending to the concerns of a private citizen?

sentences.zh: 伏願以宗廟為重，百姓為心，弘大業以嗣先軌，隆聖道以增前烈。

translations.literal: We prostrate ourselves in wishing that you take the ancestral temples as weighty and the hundred people as heart, enlarge the great enterprise to continue the prior track, and elevate the sage way to augment the former glory.
translations.idiomatic: We humbly pray that Your Majesty will hold the ancestral temples as your highest concern and the people as your heart, enlarge the great enterprise to continue your predecessors' path, and elevate the sage way to add to their glory.

sentences.zh: 愚瞽所獻，情盡於此。

translations.literal: What your blind servants offer—our feeling is exhausted here.
translations.idiomatic: This is the utmost that we your blind servants can offer.

sentences.zh: 」上乃許之。

translations.literal: The emperor then consented.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then consented.

sentences.zh: 羨之仍遜位退還私第，兄子佩之及侍中程道惠、吳興太守王韶之等並謂非宜，敦勸甚苦，復奉詔攝任。

translations.literal: Xianzhi still yielded his post and returned to his private residence; his elder brother's son Peizhi and Palace Attendant Cheng Daohui, Administrator of Wuxing Wang Shaozhi, and others all said it was improper and urged him with great earnestness; he again received an edict to hold the post provisionally.
translations.idiomatic: Xianzhi nevertheless resigned his post and retired to his private residence. His nephew Peizhi, palace attendant Cheng Daohui, administrator of Wuxing Wang Shaozhi, and others all protested that this was improper and urged him with great earnestness; he then received another edict ordering him to resume his duties provisionally.

sentences.zh: 三年正月，詔曰：「民生於三，事之如一，愛敬同極，豈惟名教，況乃施侔造物，義在加隆者乎！

translations.literal: In the first month of the third year, an edict said: "A person is born to three—serve them as one; love and reverence reach the same extreme—is this not only name and teaching, but moreover when the bestowal equals the Creator, righteousness lies in adding honor!
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the third year, an edict declared: "A person owes devotion to three—father, ruler, and teacher—and should serve them as one, with love and reverence reaching the same height. Is this not the foundation of moral teaching? How much more so when the grace bestowed equals the work of creation itself—does not righteousness demand that honor be increased?

sentences.zh: 徐羨之、傅亮、謝晦，皆因緣之才，荷恩在昔，擢自無聞，超居要重，卵翼而長，未足以譬。

translations.literal: Xu Xianzhi, Fu Liang, and Xie Hui—all are men of opportune talent who received favor in the past, plucked from obscurity to surpass and occupy crucial weight; hatched under wings and raised—this is not enough to compare.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Xianzhi, Fu Liang, and Xie Hui are all men of opportune talent who received extraordinary favor in years past—plucked from obscurity and elevated to the weightiest offices, nurtured under imperial wings from the start. No ordinary comparison suffices.

sentences.zh: 永初之季，天禍橫流，大明傾曜，四海遏密，實受顧託，任同負圖。

translations.literal: At the end of Yongchu, heaven's calamity flowed across; the great brightness tilted and its radiance fell; the four seas were stilled in mourning—they truly received the entrusted mandate, their charge equal to bearing the chart.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Yongchu reign, heaven's calamity struck; the great brightness fell and its radiance was extinguished; the four seas fell silent in mourning. These men truly received the dying emperor's entrusted mandate, a burden equal to bearing the dynastic chart upon their shoulders.

sentences.zh: 而不能竭其股肱，盡其心力，送往無復言之節，事居闕忠貞之效，將順靡記，匡救蔑聞，懷寵取容，順成失德。

translations.literal: Yet they could not exhaust their arms and legs or spend their heart's strength; seeing off the departed they lacked the rites of further speech; in service they lacked the effect of loyal steadfastness; following and smoothing had no record, correcting and saving were not heard; cherishing favor they sought accommodation, complying and completing they lost virtue.
translations.idiomatic: Yet they could not exhaust themselves in loyal service or give their utmost in devotion. In seeing off the departed emperor they failed to observe the rites of final counsel; in their conduct of affairs they showed none of the loyal steadfastness expected of them. They recorded no remonstrances when the emperor went astray, offered no rescue when disaster loomed, cherished favor and sought only to please, and by complying with his excesses allowed virtue to be lost.

sentences.zh: 雖末因懼禍，以建大策，而逞其悖心，不畏不義。

translations.literal: Though in the end, fearing calamity, they enacted the great plan, they indulged their rebellious hearts and did not fear what was unrighteous.
translations.idiomatic: Though in the end, fearing disaster for the realm, they carried out the great plan of deposition, they had long indulged their rebellious hearts and showed no fear of what was unrighteous.

sentences.zh: 播遷之始，謀肆鴆毒，至止未幾，顯行怨殺，窮凶極虐，荼酷備加，顛沛皁隸之手，告盡逆旅之館，都鄙哀愕，行路飲涕。

translations.literal: From the beginning of their wandering displacement they plotted to unleash poison; within a short time after arriving they openly carried out resentful killings; to the utmost of cruelty and extremity of tyranny, bitter torments were heaped on all; tossed into the hands of common servants, their lives ended in roadside inns; capital and countryside were struck with grief and shock, and travelers on the road swallowed their tears.
translations.idiomatic: From the moment of their forced removal from power, they plotted murder by poison; scarcely had they settled in when they openly carried out killings born of resentment. Their cruelty reached the utmost extreme, and bitter torments were heaped upon their victims, who were tossed from hand to hand among common servants until they perished in roadside inns. Capital and countryside alike were struck with grief and horror, and travelers on the road wept as they passed.

sentences.zh: 故廬陵王英秀明遠，徽風夙播，魯、衛之寄，朝野屬情。

translations.literal: Thus Prince of Luling was talented, bright, and far-seeing; his fine reputation had long been spread; the hope of Lu and Wei—court and countryside placed their feelings on him.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Luling was talented, bright, and far-seeing, his fine reputation long established; he was the hope of the realm in the manner of the lords of Lu and Wei, and court and country alike placed their hopes upon him.

sentences.zh: 羨之等暴蔑求專，忌賢畏逼，造構貝錦，成此無端，罔主蒙上，橫加流屏，矯誣朝旨，致茲禍害。

translations.literal: Xianzhi and the others were violent and contemptuous in seeking monopoly; they envied the worthy and feared pressure; they fabricated slander like brocade of shells, bringing about this groundless affair; they deceived their lord and hoodwinked their superiors, imposed banishment and exclusion, falsified and slandered court orders, and brought about this calamity.
translations.idiomatic: Xianzhi and his colleagues were violent and contemptuous in their drive for monopoly power; they envied the worthy and feared any rival; they fabricated slander as intricate as shell brocade and brought about this groundless tragedy. They deceived their sovereign and hoodwinked their superiors, imposed exile and banishment by force, falsified the court's orders, and thereby brought about this catastrophe.

sentences.zh: 寄以國命，而翦為仇讎，旬月之間，再肆鴆毒，痛感三靈，怨結人鬼。

translations.literal: Entrusted with the state's mandate, they cut them down as enemies; within a month and a fortnight they twice unleashed poison; grief touched the three spirits; resentment bound men and ghosts.
translations.idiomatic: Entrusted with the mandate of the state, they cut down their charges as enemies; within a matter of weeks they twice unleashed murder by poison. Heaven, earth, and the ancestral spirits were moved to grief; resentment bound the living and the dead alike.

sentences.zh: 自書契以來，棄常安忍，反易天明，未有如斯之甚者也。

translations.literal: Since writing and tallies began, in abandoning constants and dwelling in forbearance of cruelty, reversing and changing Heaven's brightness—never has there been anything so extreme as this.
translations.idiomatic: Since the age of writing and records began, never has anyone so abandoned moral constants, so dwelt in cruelty, or so perverted Heaven's clear mandate as these men have done.

sentences.zh: 昔子家從弑，鄭人致討；

translations.literal: In antiquity when Zijia followed in regicide, the people of Zheng brought punishment upon him;
translations.idiomatic: In antiquity, when Zijia followed his lord in regicide, the people of Zheng brought him to account;

sentences.zh: 宋肥無辜，蕩澤為戮。

translations.literal: Song Fei was innocent yet Dang Ze was executed for it.
translations.idiomatic: and when Song Fei was innocent, Dang Ze was executed in his place.

sentences.zh: 況逆亂倍於往釁，情痛深於國家，此而可容，孰不可忍！

translations.literal: How much more when rebellion and disorder double past offenses and the pain in feeling runs deeper than the state—if this can be tolerated, what cannot be endured!
translations.idiomatic: How much more so when rebellion and disorder exceed all past offenses and the anguish strikes at the very heart of the state—if this can be tolerated, what crime could not be?

sentences.zh: 即宜誅殛，告謝存亡。

translations.literal: They should immediately be executed and extinguished, announcing to the living and the dead.
translations.idiomatic: They should be executed at once, and the announcement made to living and dead alike.

sentences.zh: 而於時大事甫爾，異同紛結，匡國之勳實著，莫大之罪未彰。

translations.literal: Yet at that time the great affair had just begun; differences and agreements were tangled in confusion; the merit of restoring the state was truly manifest, and the greatest crimes were not yet revealed.
translations.idiomatic: Yet at that time the great enterprise had only just begun; factions were tangled in dispute; their merit in restoring the state was still manifest, and their greatest crimes had not yet been exposed.

sentences.zh: 是以遠酌民心，近聽輿訟，雖欲討亂，慮或難圖，故忍戚含哀，懷恥累載。

translations.literal: Therefore distantly weighing the people's hearts and near listening to public outcry, though wishing to punish the disorder, fearing it might be hard to accomplish, thus bearing sorrow and containing grief, cherishing shame for many years.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore, weighing the people's hearts from afar and listening to public outcry close at hand, I wished to punish their disorder yet feared it might prove impossible to accomplish. Thus I have borne sorrow and contained my grief, cherishing this shame for many years.

sentences.zh: 每念人生實難，情事未展，何嘗不顧影慟心，伏枕泣血。

translations.literal: Whenever I think how life is truly hard and feelings and affairs are unfulfilled, how have I not looked at my shadow and grieved in heart, lain prostrate on my pillow and wept blood?
translations.idiomatic: Whenever I reflect on how hard life truly is and how my deepest feelings remain unfulfilled, have I not gazed at my shadow and grieved in my heart, lain prostrate on my pillow and wept blood?

sentences.zh: 今逆臣之釁，彰暴遐邇，君子悲情，義徒思奮，家仇國恥，可得而雪，便命司寇，肅明典刑。

translations.literal: Now the traitors' offense is manifest, violence exposed far and near; gentlemen harbor grief and indignation, men of righteousness think to rise up; family hatred and state shame can be avenged—let the Minister of Punishments be ordered to solemnly clarify the canonical punishments.
translations.idiomatic: Now the traitors' crimes are manifest, their violence exposed far and near. Men of honor harbor grief and indignation; men of righteousness burn to act. Family hatred and national shame can at last be avenged. Let the Minister of Punishments be ordered to solemnly carry out the canonical punishments.

sentences.zh: 晦據有上流，或不即罪，朕當親率六師，為其遏防。

translations.literal: Hui holds the upper reaches and may not immediately be punished; I shall personally lead the six armies to block and guard against him.
translations.idiomatic: Hui holds the upper Yangzi region and may not submit immediately to punishment; I shall personally lead the six armies to block his path.

sentences.zh: 可遣中領軍到彥之即日電發，征北將軍檀道濟絡驛繼路，符衛軍府州以時收翦。

translations.literal: The Central Commander of the Army Dao Yanzhi may be dispatched to set out this very day like lightning; General Who Punishes the North Tan Daoji may follow relay by relay along the road; orders to the guard army, prefectures, and provinces to harvest and cut down in due time.
translations.idiomatic: The central commander of the army Dao Yanzhi shall be dispatched to set out this very day with all speed; General Who Punishes the North Tan Daoji shall follow close behind along the relay roads; and orders shall go to the guard armies, prefectures, and provinces to cut them down at the appointed time.

sentences.zh: 已命征虜將軍劉粹斷其走伏。

translations.literal: General Who Punishes the Barbarians Liu Cui has already been ordered to cut off their flight and ambush.
translations.idiomatic: General Who Punishes the Barbarians Liu Cui has already been ordered to cut off their escape routes and ambushes.

sentences.zh: 罪止元兇，餘無所問。

translations.literal: Guilt stops at the chief culprits; the rest are not to be questioned.
translations.idiomatic: Guilt shall rest only on the chief culprits; no others shall be prosecuted.

sentences.zh: 感惟永往，心情崩絕。

translations.literal: Moved by thoughts of the eternally departed, my heart and feelings are shattered to extinction.
translations.idiomatic: Moved by thoughts of those who have passed forever beyond reach, my heart is shattered.

sentences.zh: 氛霧既袪，庶幾治道。」

translations.literal: The miasma and fog having been removed, we may hope for the way of good government."
translations.idiomatic: Once the miasma has been cleared away, we may hope at last for the way of good government."

sentences.zh: 爾日詔召羨之。

translations.literal: That day an edict summoned Xianzhi.
translations.idiomatic: That same day an edict summoned Xianzhi to court.

sentences.zh: 行至西明門外，時謝晦弟皭

translations.literal: When he reached outside the Western Bright Gate, at that time Xie Hui's younger brother Xiao
translations.idiomatic: When he reached the area outside the Western Bright Gate, Xie Hui's younger brother Xiao

sentences.zh: 〈子肖反〉

translations.literal: 〈fanqie pronunciation: zi-xiao〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈pronounced zi-xiao by fanqie〉

sentences.zh: 為黃門郎，正直，報亮云：「殿內有異處分。

translations.literal: was a Yellow Gate Gentleman, upright and honest, and reported to Liang: "Within the palace there are unusual dispositions.
translations.idiomatic: was serving as a yellow gate gentleman. Upright and honest, he reported to Fu Liang: "There are unusual orders being issued within the palace.

sentences.zh: 」亮馳報羨之。

translations.literal: " Liang galloped to report to Xianzhi.
translations.idiomatic: " Liang galloped off to warn Xianzhi.

sentences.zh: 羨之回還西州，乘內人問訊車出郭，步走至新林，入陶竈中自剄死，時年六十三。

translations.literal: Xianzhi returned to Western Province, rode a palace woman's inquiry carriage out of the city, walked on foot to Xinlin, entered a pottery kiln and cut his own throat to die, aged sixty-three.
translations.idiomatic: Xianzhi turned back toward his residence in the western quarter, rode out of the city in a palace woman's inquiry carriage, then walked on foot to Xinlin, entered a pottery kiln, and cut his own throat. He was sixty-three years old.

sentences.zh: 羨之初不應召，上遣中領軍到彥之、右衛將軍王華追討。

translations.literal: Xianzhi at first did not respond to the summons; the emperor dispatched Central Commander of the Army Dao Yanzhi and General of the Right Guards Wang Hua to pursue and attack.
translations.idiomatic: Xianzhi had at first not responded to the summons, so the emperor dispatched the central commander of the army Dao Yanzhi and the general of the right guards Wang Hua to pursue him.

sentences.zh: 羨之死，野人以告，載尸付廷尉。

translations.literal: When Xianzhi died, a countryman reported it; the corpse was loaded and delivered to the Minister of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: After Xianzhi's death, a countryman reported it; his corpse was loaded onto a cart and delivered to the Minister of Justice.

sentences.zh: 子喬之，尚高祖第六女富陽公主，官至竟陵王文學。

translations.literal: His son Qiaozhi married Gaozu's sixth daughter, Princess of Fuyang, and reached the office of literary scholar to the Prince of Jingling.
translations.idiomatic: His son Qiaozhi married Gaozu's sixth daughter, the Princess of Fuyang, and rose to the post of literary scholar to the Prince of Jingling.

sentences.zh: 喬之及弟乞奴從誅。

translations.literal: Qiaozhi and his younger brother Qinu were executed along with him.
translations.idiomatic: Qiaozhi and his younger brother Qinu were executed along with him.

sentences.zh: 初，羨之年少時，嘗有一人來，謂之曰：「我是汝祖。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Xianzhi was young, a man once came and said to him: "I am your grandfather.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Xianzhi was still young, a man once came to him and said: "I am your grandfather.

sentences.zh: 」羨之因起拜之。

translations.literal: " Xianzhi thereupon rose and bowed to him.
translations.idiomatic: " Xianzhi immediately rose and bowed to him.

sentences.zh: 此人曰：「汝有貴相，而有大厄，可以錢二十八文埋宅四角，可以免災。

translations.literal: The man said: "You have a noble countenance but will suffer a great calamity; you may bury twenty-eight cash coins at the four corners of your residence to escape disaster.
translations.idiomatic: The man said: "You have the countenance of a nobleman, but you will suffer a great calamity. Bury twenty-eight cash coins at the four corners of your residence, and you may escape disaster.

sentences.zh: 過此可位極人臣。

translations.literal: Passing this you may reach the utmost rank among men and ministers."
translations.idiomatic: If you survive it, you may rise to the highest rank among men and ministers."

sentences.zh: 」後羨之隨親之縣，住在縣內，嘗暫出，而賊自後破縣；

translations.literal: Later Xianzhi followed his father to the county seat and lived within the county; he once went out briefly while bandits from behind broke into the county;
translations.idiomatic: Later, when Xianzhi accompanied his father to a county post and lived within the county seat, he once stepped out briefly while bandits attacked the county from behind;

sentences.zh: 縣內人無免者，雞犬亦盡，唯羨之在外獲全。

translations.literal: no one within the county escaped, chickens and dogs were also all gone—only Xianzhi, being outside, was preserved whole.
translations.idiomatic: not a soul within the county escaped, and even the chickens and dogs were slaughtered to the last—only Xianzhi, being outside at the time, was spared.

sentences.zh: 隨從兄履之為臨海樂安縣，嘗行經山中，見黑龍長丈餘，頭有角，前兩足皆具，無後足，曳尾而行。

translations.literal: His cousin Lüzhi served as magistrate of Le'an in Linhai; once traveling through the mountains he saw a black dragon more than a zhang long, with horns on its head, both forelegs complete, no hind legs, dragging its tail as it went.
translations.idiomatic: His cousin Lüzhi served as magistrate of Le'an in Linhai commandery. Once while traveling through the mountains he saw a black dragon more than ten feet long, with horns on its head, both forelegs complete but no hind legs, dragging its tail as it moved.

sentences.zh: 及拜司空，守關將入，彗星晨見危南。

translations.literal: When he was appointed Minister of Works, guarding the pass about to enter, a comet was seen at dawn south of Wei.
translations.idiomatic: When he was appointed minister of works and was about to pass through the palace gate, a comet appeared at dawn south of the Wei asterism.

sentences.zh: 又當拜時，雙鶴集太極東鴟尾鳴喚。

translations.literal: Again when he was about to receive appointment, a pair of cranes gathered at the eastern Owl Tail of the Supreme Ultimate and cried calling.
translations.idiomatic: Again, at the time of his appointment, a pair of cranes gathered at the eastern Owl Tail gate of the Supreme Ultimate palace and cried out.

sentences.zh: 兄子佩之，輕薄好利，高祖以其姻戚，累加寵任，為丹陽尹，吳郡太守。

translations.literal: His elder brother's son Peizhi was frivolous and fond of profit; Gaozu because of the marriage connection repeatedly added favor and trust, making him Governor of Danyang and Administrator of Wu commandery.
translations.idiomatic: His nephew Peizhi was frivolous and greedy for profit. Because of the family connection by marriage, Gaozu repeatedly favored and trusted him, appointing him governor of Danyang and administrator of Wu commandery.

sentences.zh: 景平初，以羨之秉權，頗豫政事。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jingping, because Xianzhi held power, he participated considerably in government affairs.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Jingping reign, with Xianzhi holding power, Peizhi participated considerably in government affairs.

sentences.zh: 與王韶之、程道惠、中書舍人邢安泰、潘盛相結黨與。

translations.literal: He formed a faction with Wang Shaozhi, Cheng Daohui, and Palace Secretariat attendants Xing Antai and Pan Sheng.
translations.idiomatic: He formed a faction with Wang Shaozhi, Cheng Daohui, and the palace attendants Xing Antai and Pan Sheng.

sentences.zh: 時謝晦久病，連灸，不堪見客。

translations.literal: At that time Xie Hui had long been ill, undergoing repeated moxibustion, unable to receive guests.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Xie Hui had long been ill, undergoing repeated courses of moxibustion, and was unable to receive visitors.

sentences.zh: 佩之等疑其託疾有異圖，與韶之、道惠同載詣傅亮，稱羨之意，欲令亮作詔誅之。

translations.literal: Peizhi and the others suspected he was feigning illness with a different plot; together with Shaozhi and Daohui they rode in the same carriage to Fu Liang, stating Xianzhi's intent, wishing to have Liang draft an edict to execute him.
translations.idiomatic: Peizhi and his associates suspected that Xie Hui was feigning illness as cover for some other plot. Together with Shaozhi and Daohui they rode to Fu Liang's residence, stated Xianzhi's wishes, and asked Liang to draft an edict ordering Xie Hui's execution.

sentences.zh: 亮答以為：「己等三人，同受顧命，豈可相殘戮！

translations.literal: Liang replied: "We three alike received the entrusted mandate—how can we slaughter one another!
translations.idiomatic: Liang replied: "We three alike received the dying emperor's entrusted mandate—how can we slaughter one another!

sentences.zh: 若諸君果行此事，便當角巾步出掖門耳。

translations.literal: If you gentlemen truly carry out this affair, I shall simply tie a kerchief and walk out through the Side Gate."
translations.idiomatic: If you gentlemen truly carry this through, I shall simply tie on a scholar's kerchief and walk out through the side gate."

sentences.zh: 」佩之等乃止。

translations.literal: Peizhi and the others then stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Peizhi and his associates then abandoned the plan.

sentences.zh: 羨之既誅，太祖特宥佩之，免官而已。

translations.literal: After Xianzhi was executed, Taizu specially pardoned Peizhi, merely removing his office.
translations.idiomatic: After Xianzhi was executed, Taizu specially pardoned Peizhi, merely stripping him of his offices.

sentences.zh: 其年冬，佩之又結殿中監茅亨謀反，並告前寧州刺史應襲，以亨為兗州，襲為豫州。

translations.literal: That winter Peizhi again joined Palace Interior Supervisor Mao Heng in plotting rebellion, and together informed former Inspector of Ning Province Ying Xi, making Heng governor of Yanzhou and Xi governor of Yuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: That winter Peizhi again joined the palace interior supervisor Mao Heng in plotting rebellion, and together they enlisted the former inspector of Ning Province Ying Xi, assigning Heng to Yanzhou and Xi to Yuzhou.

sentences.zh: 亨密以聞，襲亦告司徒王弘。

translations.literal: Heng secretly reported it; Xi also informed Minister of Education Wang Hong.
translations.idiomatic: Heng secretly reported the plot to the throne; Xi also informed the minister of education Wang Hong.

sentences.zh: 佩之聚黨百餘人，殺牛犒賜，條牒時人，竝相署置，期明年正會，於殿中作亂。

translations.literal: Peizhi gathered a faction of more than a hundred men, slaughtered cattle to reward them, listed and registered people of the time, all mutually appointing one another, setting the first month assembly of the next year to make disorder in the palace.
translations.idiomatic: Peizhi gathered a faction of more than a hundred men, slaughtered cattle to feast them, drew up lists of contemporaries and mutually assigned them posts, planning to stage a coup in the palace at the New Year's assembly of the following year.

sentences.zh: 未及數日，收斬之。

translations.literal: Before several days had passed, he was arrested and beheaded.
translations.idiomatic: Within a few days he was arrested and beheaded.

sentences.zh: 傅亮，字季友，北地靈州人也。

translations.literal: Fu Liang, styled Jiyou, was a man of Lingzhou in Beidi.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Liang, whose style was Jiyou, came from Lingzhou in Beidi commandery.

sentences.zh: 祖咸，司隸校尉。

translations.literal: His grandfather Xian was Colonel of the Secretariat for the Capital Region.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Xian had served as colonel of the secretariat for the capital region.

sentences.zh: 父瑗，以學業知名，位至安成太守。

translations.literal: His father Yuan was renowned for scholarly learning and reached the post of Administrator of Ancheng.
translations.idiomatic: His father Yuan was renowned for scholarly learning and rose to the post of administrator of Ancheng.

sentences.zh: 瑗與郗超善，超嘗造瑗，瑗見其二子迪及亮。

translations.literal: Yuan was friendly with Xi Chao; Chao once visited Yuan, and Yuan had him see his two sons Di and Liang.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan was on friendly terms with Xi Chao. Chao once visited Yuan, and Yuan introduced him to his two sons Di and Liang.

sentences.zh: 亮年四五歲，超令人解亮衣，使左右持去，初無吝色。

translations.literal: Liang was four or five years old; Chao had someone remove Liang's clothes and ordered attendants to carry them away—at first there was no sign of reluctance.
translations.idiomatic: Liang was only four or five years old. Chao had someone remove Liang's clothes and ordered his attendants to carry them away; the boy showed not the slightest reluctance.

sentences.zh: 超謂瑗曰：「卿小兒才名位宦，當遠逾於兄。

translations.literal: Chao said to Yuan: "Your young son in talent, fame, rank, and office should far surpass his elder brother.
translations.idiomatic: Chao said to Yuan: "Your younger son in talent, fame, rank, and office will far surpass his elder brother.

sentences.zh: 然保家傳祚，終在大者。

translations.literal: Yet in preserving the family and transmitting the fief, in the end it will be the elder."
translations.idiomatic: Yet in preserving the family and transmitting its estate, the elder brother will have the final word."

sentences.zh: 」迪字長猷，亦儒學，官至五兵尚書。

translations.literal: Di, styled Changyou, also studied Confucian learning and reached the office of Director of the Five Weapons.
translations.idiomatic: Di, whose style was Changyou, also pursued Confucian learning and rose to the post of director of the five weapons.

sentences.zh: 永初二年卒，追贈太常。

translations.literal: He died in the second year of Yongchu and was posthumously given the Grand Master of Ceremonies.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the second year of Yongchu and was posthumously appointed grand master of ceremonies.

sentences.zh: 亮博涉經史，尤善文詞。

translations.literal: Liang broadly covered the classics and histories and was especially skilled in literary composition.
translations.idiomatic: Liang had broad knowledge of the classics and histories and was especially skilled in literary composition.

sentences.zh: 初為建威參軍，桓謙中軍行參軍。

translations.literal: He first served as staff officer of the army that establishes might and as traveling staff officer on Huan Qian's central army.
translations.idiomatic: He first served as staff officer of the army that establishes might and as traveling staff officer on Huan Qian's central army staff.

sentences.zh: 桓玄篡位，聞其博學有文采，選為秘書郎，欲令整正秘閣，未及拜而玄敗。

translations.literal: When Huan Xuan usurped the throne, hearing of his broad learning and literary talent, he was selected as Secretariat Gentleman, intending to have him put in order the secret archives—but before he could assume the post Xuan was defeated.
translations.idiomatic: When Huan Xuan usurped the throne, hearing of Liang's broad learning and literary talent, he selected him as secretariat gentleman with the intention of having him reorganize the imperial archives—but before Liang could assume the post, Xuan was overthrown.

sentences.zh: 義旗初，丹陽尹孟昶以為建威參軍。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the righteous banner, Governor of Danyang Meng Chang made him staff officer of the army that establishes might.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the righteous army's campaign, the governor of Danyang Meng Chang appointed him staff officer of the army that establishes might.

sentences.zh: 義熙元年，除員外散騎侍郎，直西省，典掌詔命。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yixi he was made Extraordinary Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry, serving in the Western Secretariat and presiding over edicts and orders.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Yixi (405), he was appointed extraordinary attendant of the scattered cavalry, serving in the western secretariat with charge over edicts and orders.

sentences.zh: 轉領軍長史，以中書郎滕演代之。

translations.literal: He was transferred to chief clerk of the army command; Secretariat Gentleman Teng Yan replaced him.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to chief clerk of the army command, and the secretariat gentleman Teng Yan replaced him in his former post.

sentences.zh: 亮未拜，遭母憂，服闋，為劉毅撫軍記室參軍，又補領軍司馬。

translations.literal: Liang had not yet assumed the post when he encountered his mother's mourning; after the mourning period ended he became recording staff officer on Liu Yi's pacification army and was also assigned as marshal of the army command.
translations.idiomatic: Liang had not yet assumed the post when his mother died. After the mourning period ended, he became recording staff officer on Liu Yi's pacification army and was also assigned as marshal of the army command.

sentences.zh: 七年，遷散騎侍郎，復代演直西省。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he was moved to Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry and again replaced Yan in the Western Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year he was promoted to attendant of the scattered cavalry and again replaced Teng Yan in the western secretariat.

sentences.zh: 仍轉中書黃門侍郎，直西省如故。

translations.literal: He was then transferred to Secretariat Yellow Gate Attendant with service in the Western Secretariat as before.
translations.idiomatic: He was then transferred to secretariat yellow gate attendant, continuing to serve in the western secretariat as before.

sentences.zh: 高祖以其久直勤勞，欲以為東陽郡，先以語迪，迪大喜告亮。

translations.literal: Gaozu because of his long service and diligent labor wished to make him Administrator of Dongyang; he first told Di, and Di in great joy told Liang.
translations.idiomatic: Because of his long and diligent service, Gaozu wished to appoint him administrator of Dongyang. He first told Di, who was overjoyed and told Liang.

sentences.zh: 亮不答，即馳見高祖曰：「伏聞恩旨，賜擬東陽，家貧忝祿，私計為幸。

translations.literal: Liang did not reply but immediately galloped to see Gaozu and said: "I have heard the gracious intent to grant me Dongyang; my family is poor and I am honored by salary—privately I count it fortune.
translations.idiomatic: Liang made no reply but immediately galloped to see Gaozu and said: "I have heard of Your Majesty's gracious intent to appoint me to Dongyang. My family is poor, and I would be honored to receive such a salary—privately I count it good fortune.

sentences.zh: 但憑廕之願，實結本心，乞歸天宇，不樂外出。

translations.literal: But the wish to rely on shade and favor truly knots my original heart; I beg to return to the heavenly court and do not delight in going outside."
translations.idiomatic: But my deepest wish has always been to serve at court; I beg to remain under heaven's canopy and have no desire to serve in the provinces."

sentences.zh: 」高祖笑曰：「謂卿之須祿耳，若能如此，甚協所望。

translations.literal: " Gaozu laughed and said: "I thought you needed the salary—but if you can be like this, it greatly accords with what I hoped."
translations.idiomatic: " Gaozu laughed and said: "I thought you needed the salary—but if you truly feel this way, it accords perfectly with what I hoped."

sentences.zh: 」會西討司馬休之，以為太尉從事中郎，掌記室。

translations.literal: When the western campaign against Sima Xiuzhi arose, he was made Attendant Gentleman on the Grand Commander's staff, in charge of the recording office.
translations.idiomatic: When the western campaign against Sima Xiuzhi arose, he was appointed attendant gentleman on the Grand Commander's staff, in charge of the recording office.

sentences.zh: 以太尉參軍羊徽為中書郎，代直西省。

translations.literal: Grand Commander staff officer Yang Hui was made Secretariat Gentleman to replace him in the Western Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Commander's staff officer Yang Hui was made secretariat gentleman to replace him in the western secretariat.

sentences.zh: 亮從征關、洛，還至彭城。

translations.literal: Liang followed the campaign to Guan and Luo and returned to Pengcheng.
translations.idiomatic: Liang followed the campaign to the Guan and Luo regions and returned to Pengcheng.

sentences.zh: 宋國初建，令書除侍中，領世子中庶子。

translations.literal: When the Song state was first established, an order appointed him Palace Attendant and Concurrent Junior Tutor to the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: When the Song state was first established, an order appointed him palace attendant and concurrent junior tutor to the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 徙中書令，領中庶子如故。

translations.literal: He was moved to Director of the Secretariat with his junior tutorship unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: He was then promoted to director of the Secretariat, retaining his post as junior tutor.

sentences.zh: 從還壽陽。

translations.literal: He followed the return to Shouyang.
translations.idiomatic: He accompanied the court on its return to Shouyang.

sentences.zh: 高祖有受禪意，而難於發言，乃集朝臣宴飲，從容言曰：「桓玄暴篡，鼎命已移，我首唱大義，復興皇室，南征北伐，平定四海，功成業著，遂荷九錫。

translations.literal: Gaozu had the intent to receive the abdication but found it hard to speak; he gathered court officials for a drinking feast and said at ease: "Huan Xuan violently usurped; the tripod mandate already shifted; I first raised the great principle, revived the imperial house, campaigned south and north, pacified the four seas; merit accomplished and enterprise manifest, I then bore the nine bestowals.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu intended to accept the abdication of the Jin throne but found it difficult to broach the subject. He gathered the court officials for a feast and said at his ease: "Huan Xuan violently usurped the throne, and the mandate of heaven shifted. I was the first to raise the banner of righteousness and revive the imperial house. I campaigned south and north and pacified the four seas. My merit accomplished and my enterprise manifest, I have received the nine bestowals.

sentences.zh: 今年將衰暮，崇極如此，物戒盛滿，非可久安。

translations.literal: This year I approach decline and evening; honor has reached such extremity; things warn against fullness at the peak—it cannot long be secure.
translations.idiomatic: This year I approach old age, and my honors have reached such heights. All things warn against fullness at the peak—it cannot long endure.

sentences.zh: 今欲奉還爵位，歸老京師。

translations.literal: Now I wish to offer back rank and fief and retire old in the capital."
translations.idiomatic: Now I wish to return my rank and fief and retire to old age in the capital."

sentences.zh: 」群臣唯盛稱功德，莫曉此意。

translations.literal: The officials only lavishly praised his merit and virtue; none understood this intent.
translations.idiomatic: The officials could only lavish praise on his merit and virtue; none understood what he truly meant.

sentences.zh: 日晚坐散，亮還外，乃悟旨，而宮門已閉；

translations.literal: When evening came the session dispersed; Liang returned outside and then grasped the intent—but the palace gates were already closed;
translations.idiomatic: When evening came the session dispersed. Liang returned to his quarters and only then grasped Gaozu's true intent—but the palace gates were already closed.

sentences.zh: 亮於是叩扉請見，高祖即開門見之。

translations.literal: Liang thereupon knocked on the door and requested an audience; Gaozu immediately opened the gate and received him.
translations.idiomatic: Liang thereupon knocked on the gate and requested an audience; Gaozu immediately opened it and received him.

sentences.zh: 亮入便曰：「臣暫宜還都。

translations.literal: Liang entered and at once said: "Your servant should for the moment return to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Liang entered and at once said: "Your servant should return to the capital for the time being.

sentences.zh: 」高祖達解此意，無復他言，直云：「須幾人自送？

translations.literal: " Gaozu thoroughly understood this intent and had no further words; he simply said: "How many men are needed to escort you?"
translations.idiomatic: " Gaozu immediately understood and said nothing more, asking simply: "How many men will you need as escort?"

sentences.zh: 」亮曰：「須數十人便足。

translations.literal: " Liang said: "Several tens of men will suffice."
translations.idiomatic: " Liang replied: "Several dozen will be sufficient."

sentences.zh: 」於是即便奉辭。

translations.literal: He thereupon immediately took leave.
translations.idiomatic: He thereupon immediately took his leave.

sentences.zh: 亮既出，已夜，見長星竟天。

translations.literal: After Liang had gone out, it was already night; he saw a long comet spanning the sky.
translations.idiomatic: After Liang had departed, night had fallen, and he saw a long comet stretching across the sky.

sentences.zh: 亮拊髀曰：「我常不信天文，今始驗矣！

translations.literal: Liang slapped his thigh and said: "I have always disbelieved astronomy—now it is first verified!
translations.idiomatic: Liang slapped his thigh and exclaimed: "I have always disbelieved in astrology—now I am convinced!

sentences.zh: 」至都，即徵高祖入輔。

translations.literal: " Reaching the capital, he immediately summoned Gaozu to enter as assistant.
translations.idiomatic: " Reaching the capital, he immediately set in motion the summons for Gaozu to enter and assume the regency.

sentences.zh: 永初元年，遷太子詹事，中書令如故。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yongchu he was moved to Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent with his directorship of the Secretariat unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Yongchu (420), he was promoted to grand tutor of the heir apparent, retaining his post as director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 以佐命功，封建城縣公，食邑二千戶。

translations.literal: For merit in assisting the mandate he was enfeoffed as Duke of Jiancheng county with a fief of two thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: For his merit in assisting the founding mandate, he was enfeoffed as Duke of Jiancheng with a fief of two thousand households.

sentences.zh: 入直中書省，專典詔命。

translations.literal: He entered and served directly in the Secretariat, exclusively presiding over edicts and orders.
translations.idiomatic: He served directly in the secretariat, with exclusive charge over edicts and orders.

sentences.zh: 以亮任總國權，聽於省見客。

translations.literal: Because Liang held overall state authority, he was permitted to receive guests within the secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Because Liang held overall authority over state affairs, he was permitted to receive guests within the secretariat.

sentences.zh: 神虎門外，每旦車常數百兩。

translations.literal: Outside the Divine Tiger Gate, each morning carriages regularly numbered in the hundreds.
translations.idiomatic: Outside the Divine Tiger Gate, hundreds of carriages gathered every morning.

sentences.zh: 高祖登庸之始，文筆皆是記室參軍滕演；

translations.literal: At the beginning when Gaozu rose to power, all literary documents were by recording staff officer Teng Yan;
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Gaozu's rise to power, all official documents were drafted by the recording staff officer Teng Yan;

sentences.zh: 北征廣固，悉委長史王誕；

translations.literal: on the northern expedition to Guanggu, all were entrusted to chief clerk Wang Dan;
translations.idiomatic: during the northern expedition against Guanggu, all were entrusted to the chief clerk Wang Dan;

sentences.zh: 自此後至於受命，表策文誥，皆亮辭也。

translations.literal: from this afterward until receiving the mandate, memorials, proclamations, documents, and edicts were all Liang's compositions.
translations.idiomatic: from that point until Gaozu received the mandate of heaven, all memorials, proclamations, documents, and edicts were composed by Liang.

sentences.zh: 演字彥將，南陽西鄂人，官至黃門郎，秘書監。

translations.literal: Yan, styled Yanjiang, was a man of Xi'e in Nanyang; he reached the posts of Gentleman of the Yellow Gate and Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Teng Yan, whose style was Yanjiang, came from Xi'e in Nanyang commandery and rose to gentleman of the yellow gate and director of the secretariat.

sentences.zh: 義熙八年卒。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Yixi he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the eighth year of Yixi (412).

sentences.zh: 二年，亮轉尚書僕射，中書令、詹事如故。

translations.literal: In the second year, Liang was transferred to Vice Director of the Secretariat; his posts as Director of the Secretariat and Grand Tutor remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Yongchu (421), Fu Liang was promoted to vice director of the Secretariat, retaining his posts as director of the Secretariat and grand tutor of the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 明年，高祖不豫，與徐羨之、謝晦並受顧命，給班劍二十人。

translations.literal: The next year Gaozu was unwell; together with Xu Xianzhi and Xie Hui he jointly received the dying charge, and was granted twenty guard halberds.
translations.idiomatic: The following year, when Gaozu fell gravely ill, he was named together with Xu Xianzhi and Xie Hui among those entrusted with the dying emperor's final mandate, and was granted twenty guard halberds.

sentences.zh: 少帝即位，進為中書監，尚書令。

translations.literal: When Emperor Shao ascended the throne, Liang was advanced to Director of the Secretariat and Minister of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Shao took the throne, Fu Liang was promoted to director of the Secretariat and minister of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 景平二年，領護軍將軍。

translations.literal: In the second year of Jingping he concurrently held the post of General Who Protects the Army.
