translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Jingping (424), he also took charge as general who protects the army.

sentences.zh: 少帝廢，亮率行臺至江陵奉迎太祖。

translations.literal: When Emperor Shao was deposed, Liang led the traveling office to Jiangling to welcome and escort Taizu.
translations.idiomatic: After Emperor Shao was deposed, Fu Liang led the traveling secretariat to Jiangling to welcome and escort Taizu (Emperor Wen).

sentences.zh: 既至，立行門於江陵城南，題曰「大司馬門。

translations.literal: When they had arrived, he established a traveling gate south of Jiangling city and inscribed it "Great Marshal Gate."
translations.idiomatic: On arrival he set up a ceremonial gate south of Jiangling and inscribed it "Gate of the Great Marshal."

sentences.zh: 」率行臺百僚詣門拜表，威儀禮容甚盛。

translations.literal: He led the hundred officials of the traveling office to the gate to present a memorial in obeisance; the majesty of ritual and bearing was very great.
translations.idiomatic: He then led the traveling office's officials to the gate to bow and submit their memorial, with magnificent ceremony and decorum.

sentences.zh: 太祖將下，引見亮，哭慟甚，哀動左右。

translations.literal: When Taizu was about to descend, he summoned Liang for an audience; he wept with extreme grief, and his sorrow moved those on either side.
translations.idiomatic: As Taizu was about to come down, he received Fu Liang in audience and wept bitterly, his grief moving all who stood beside him.

sentences.zh: 既而問義真及少帝薨廢本末，悲號嗚咽，侍側者莫能仰視。

translations.literal: Then he asked the full circumstances of Yifu's death and Emperor Shao's deposition and demise; he wailed and sobbed, and those attending at his side could not look up at him.
translations.idiomatic: He then asked for the full story of Prince Yifu's death and Emperor Shao's deposition and demise, wailing and sobbing until those beside him dared not raise their eyes.

sentences.zh: 亮流汗沾背，不能答。

translations.literal: Liang's sweat soaked his back; he could not answer.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Liang, sweat streaming down his back, could not reply.

sentences.zh: 於是布腹心於到彥之、王華等，深自結納。

translations.literal: Thereupon he laid bare his innermost thoughts to Dao Yanzhi, Wang Hua, and others, and bound himself to them in deep alliance.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon he confided his innermost thoughts to Dao Yanzhi, Wang Hua, and others and forged close ties with them.

sentences.zh: 太祖登阼，加散騎常侍、左光祿大夫、開府儀同三司，本官悉如故。

translations.literal: When Taizu ascended the throne, Liang was given the additional titles of Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry, Left Grand Master of Splendor, and Bearer of Credentials Equal to the Three Excellencies; all his original offices remained unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: When Taizu took the throne, Fu Liang was further appointed regular attendant of the scattered cavalry, left grand master of splendor, and bearer of credentials equal to the Three Excellencies, while all his existing offices remained unchanged.

sentences.zh: 司空府文武即為左光祿府。

translations.literal: The civil and military staff of the Minister of Works office became the staff of the Left Grand Master of Splendor office.
translations.idiomatic: The civil and military staff of his former minister of works office became the staff of his left grand master of splendor establishment.

sentences.zh: 又進爵始興郡公，食邑四千戶，固讓進封。

translations.literal: He was further advanced in enfeoffment to Duke of Shixing commandery with a fief of four thousand households, but firmly declined further promotion in rank.
translations.idiomatic: He was further enfeoffed as Duke of Shixing with a fief of four thousand households, but firmly declined the additional honors.

sentences.zh: 元嘉三年，太祖欲誅亮，先呼入見；

translations.literal: In the third year of Yuanjia, Taizu wished to execute Liang and first summoned him for an audience;
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Yuanjia (426), Taizu intended to execute Fu Liang and first summoned him to audience;

sentences.zh: 省內密有報之者，亮辭以嫂病篤，求暫還家。

translations.literal: within the secretariat someone secretly reported to him; Liang declined on the grounds that his sister-in-law's illness was grave and begged temporary leave to return home.
translations.idiomatic: someone within the secretariat secretly warned him. Fu Liang pleaded that his sister-in-law was gravely ill and begged leave to return home briefly.

sentences.zh: 遣信報徐羨之，因乘車出郭門，騎馬奔兄迪墓。

translations.literal: He sent a messenger to report to Xu Xianzhi, then rode in a carriage out the outer city gate, mounted a horse, and raced to his elder brother Di's tomb.
translations.idiomatic: He sent word to Xu Xianzhi, rode out through the outer gate, then mounted a horse and galloped to his elder brother Di's tomb.

sentences.zh: 屯騎校尉郭泓收付廷尉，伏誅。

translations.literal: Colonel of Garrison Cavalry Guo Hong seized him and delivered him to the Minister of Justice; he was executed by beheading.
translations.idiomatic: Colonel of garrison cavalry Guo Hong arrested him and handed him over to the minister of justice, where he was beheaded.

sentences.zh: 時年五十三。

translations.literal: He was then fifty-three years of age.
translations.idiomatic: He was fifty-three years old.

sentences.zh: 初至廣莫門，上遣中書舍人以詔書示亮，並謂曰：「以公江陵之誠，當使諸子無恙。

translations.literal: When he first reached the Broad Mo Gate, the emperor sent a Secretariat Gentleman to show Liang the edict, and also said to him: "For your loyalty at Jiangling, your sons shall be kept unharmed."
translations.idiomatic: When he first reached the Broad Mo Gate, the emperor sent a secretariat gentleman to show Fu Liang the edict, adding: "For your loyalty at Jiangling, your sons shall come to no harm."

sentences.zh: 」初，亮見世路屯險，著論名曰《演慎》，曰：

translations.literal: Earlier, Liang saw that the path of the age was perilous and blocked, and composed a treatise entitled Practicing Caution, saying:
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, seeing the times treacherous and perilous, Fu Liang had written a treatise entitled "Practicing Caution," which begins:

sentences.zh: 大道有言，慎終如始，則無敗事矣。

translations.literal: The Great Way has said: "Be careful at the end as at the beginning, and there will be no failed undertakings."
translations.idiomatic: The Great Way says: "Be as careful at the end as at the beginning, and you will have no failed undertakings."

sentences.zh: 《易》曰：「括囊無咎。

translations.literal: The Changes says: "Tie the sack—no blame."
translations.idiomatic: The Book of Changes says: "Bind the sack shut—no blame."

sentences.zh: 」慎不害也。

translations.literal: Caution does no harm.
translations.idiomatic: Caution does no harm.

sentences.zh: 又曰：「藉之用茅，何咎之有。

translations.literal: It also says: "Spread mao grass beneath—what blame could there be?"
translations.idiomatic: It also says: "Lay mao grass beneath—what blame could there be?"

sentences.zh: 」慎之至也。

translations.literal: This is caution at its utmost.
translations.idiomatic: That is caution carried to its utmost.

sentences.zh: 文王小心，《大雅》詠其多福；

translations.literal: King Wen was cautious; the Da Ya hymns praise his abundant blessings;
translations.idiomatic: King Wen was ever cautious; the Da Ya hymns celebrate his abundant blessings;

sentences.zh: 仲由好勇，馮河貽其苦箴。

translations.literal: Zhong You loved valor; fording the river earned him bitter admonition.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong You loved boldness; wading the river brought him stern rebuke.

sentences.zh: 《虞書》著慎身之譽，周廟銘陛坐之側。

translations.literal: The Documents of Yu record praise for cultivating the person with caution; the Zhou ancestral temple bore inscriptions beside the throne steps.
translations.idiomatic: The Documents of Yu praise cautious self-cultivation; the Zhou ancestral temple bore inscriptions beside the throne.

sentences.zh: 因斯以談，所以保身全德，其莫尚於慎乎！

translations.literal: From these examples one may discuss how to preserve the person and perfect virtue—surely nothing surpasses caution!
translations.idiomatic: From these examples one sees that to preserve oneself and perfect one's virtue, nothing surpasses caution.

sentences.zh: 夫四道好謙，三才忌滿，祥萃虛室，鬼瞰高屋，豐屋有蔀家之災，鼎食無百年之貴。

translations.literal: The Four Ways love humility; the Three Powers abhor fullness; auspicious omens gather in empty rooms, and ghosts peer into lofty houses. Sumptuous dwellings bring the calamity of a darkened household; tripod-fed nobility lack a century of eminence.
translations.idiomatic: The Four Ways love humility; the Three Powers abhor excess; good fortune gathers in humble rooms while ghosts stare down from high roofs. Grand houses invite ruin for the household; nobles who feast from tripods rarely keep their glory for a hundred years.

sentences.zh: 然而徇欲厚生者，忽而不戒；

translations.literal: Yet those who pursue desires and thick living heedlessly neglect warning;
translations.idiomatic: Yet those who chase desire and lavish living heed no warning;

sentences.zh: 知進忘退者，曾莫之懲。

translations.literal: those who know advance and forget retreat are never corrected.
translations.idiomatic: those who know only advance and forget retreat are never corrected.

sentences.zh: 前車已摧，後鑾不息，乘危以庶安，行險而徼幸，於是有顛墜覆亡之禍，殘生夭命之釁。

translations.literal: The forward chariot is already wrecked, yet the rear team does not rest; riding danger hoping for safety, walking peril while trusting luck—thus come calamities of toppling and ruin, and omens of shortened life and untimely death.
translations.idiomatic: The lead chariot is already wrecked, yet the rear team presses on; men ride danger hoping for safety and walk peril trusting luck—hence the calamity of collapse and ruin, the omen of life cut short.

sentences.zh: 其故何哉？

translations.literal: What is the reason?
translations.idiomatic: Why is this so?

sentences.zh: 流溺忘反，而以身輕於物也。

translations.literal: Drifting and drowning, they forget to return, and treat their persons as lighter than external things.
translations.idiomatic: They drift and drown, forget to turn back, and value things above their own lives.

sentences.zh: 故昔之君子，同名爵於香餌，故傾危不及；

translations.literal: Thus the gentlemen of old equated fame and rank with fragrant bait, and so did not reach ruin;
translations.idiomatic: Thus the gentlemen of old equated fame and rank with fragrant bait, and so escaped ruin;

sentences.zh: 思憂患而豫防，則針石無用。

translations.literal: they pondered peril beforehand and guarded against it, and so had no need of the needle and stone of medicine.
translations.idiomatic: they foresaw trouble and guarded against it, and so never needed the physician's needle and stone.

sentences.zh: 洪流壅於涓涓，合拱挫於纖蘖，介焉是式，色斯而舉，悟高鳥以風逝，鑒醴酒而投紱。

translations.literal: Great floods are dammed by trickling streams; arms-span trees are broken by tiny shoots. Taking the upright as their model, they rose at the first sign of color; they understood from the high bird that vanishes with the wind, and took wine as a mirror and cast off their sashes.
translations.idiomatic: Great floods are blocked by trickles; trees an arms-span round are felled by tender shoots. They took the upright as model and rose at the first warning; they learned from the high bird that flees on the wind, and seeing wine offered, cast off office and went away.

sentences.zh: 夫豈敝著而後謀通，患結而後思復云爾而已哉！

translations.literal: How could it be only after garments are worn out that one plots escape, and only after calamity is knotted that one thinks of return—nothing more than that!
translations.idiomatic: Surely it was not only after their robes were worn threadbare that they planned escape, nor only after disaster had struck that they thought of returning—nothing more than that!

sentences.zh: 故《詩》曰：「慎爾侯度，用戒不虞。

translations.literal: Thus the Odes say: "Be careful in your lord's measure, and guard against the unforeseen."
translations.idiomatic: Thus the Odes say: "Be careful in your lord's measure, and guard against the unforeseen."

sentences.zh: 」言防萌也。

translations.literal: This speaks of guarding against what is nascent.
translations.idiomatic: This speaks of nipping trouble in the bud.

sentences.zh: 夫單以營內喪表，張以治外失中，齊、秦有守一之敗，偏恃無兼濟之功，冰炭滌於胸心，岩牆絕於四體。

translations.literal: Shan, by cultivating inwardness, lost outward expression; Zhang, by governing outward affairs, lost the mean. Qi and Qin had failures from clinging to one thing; partial reliance achieves no comprehensive success. Ice and charcoal wash the breast, and cliff walls cut off the four limbs.
translations.idiomatic: Shan, cultivating inwardness alone, lost his outward bearing; Zhang, governing outward affairs alone, lost the mean. Qi and Qin failed from clinging to a single path; one-sided reliance cannot achieve comprehensive success. Ice and charcoal alternate in the heart, and cliff walls sever the four limbs.

sentences.zh: 夫然，故形神偕全，表裏寧一，營魄內澄，百骸外固，邪氣不能襲，憂患不能及，然可以語至而言極矣！

translations.literal: Thus form and spirit are together preserved, inner and outer are at peace as one, the animating soul is clarified within, the hundred bones are secured without; no evil qi can assail, no peril can reach—only then may one speak of the utmost and reach the extreme!
translations.idiomatic: Only then are body and spirit preserved together, inner and outer at one; the soul clarified within, the frame secured without—evil cannot assail, trouble cannot reach. Only then may one speak of the utmost and reach the extreme.

sentences.zh: 夫以嵇子之抗心希古，絕羈獨放，五難之根既拔，立生之道無累，人患殆乎盡矣。

translations.literal: As for Master Ji, with a defiant heart he aspired to antiquity, broke all reins and wandered alone—the roots of the Five Difficulties were already uprooted, the Way of establishing life was without encumbrance; human peril was nearly exhausted.
translations.idiomatic: Consider Ji Kang: with a defiant heart he aspired to antiquity, broke every rein and wandered alone—the roots of the Five Difficulties were uprooted, the way of life was unburdened; human peril was nearly exhausted.

sentences.zh: 徒以忽防於鍾、呂，肆言於禹、湯，禍機發於豪端，逸翩鎩於垂舉。

translations.literal: He only neglected caution regarding Zhong and Lü, and spoke freely of Yu and Tang; the engine of calamity was triggered at a hair's breadth, and his soaring wings were broken just as he was about to rise.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he neglected caution toward Zhong and Lü and spoke freely of Yu and Tang; disaster sparked at a hair's breadth, and his soaring wings were clipped just as he was lifting off.

sentences.zh: 觀夫貽書良友，則匹厚味於甘鴆，囗囗囗囗囗囗囗囗其懼患也，若無轡而乘奔，其慎禍也，猶履冰而臨谷。

translations.literal: Observing his letters to good friends, he matched rich flavor to sweet poison; [text lost] their fear of peril was like riding a galloping horse without reins; their caution against calamity was like treading ice while facing a ravine.
translations.idiomatic: When one sees his letters to close friends, he likens rich favors to sweet poison; his dread of peril is like riding a runaway horse without reins, and his caution against disaster like walking on ice above a chasm.

sentences.zh: 或振褐高棲，揭竿獨往，或保約違豐，安於卑位。

translations.literal: Some shake out coarse robes and dwell on high perches; some raise a pole and go alone; some keep to modest covenants and reject abundance, content in humble stations.
translations.idiomatic: Some shake out rough robes and dwell apart on high; some take up a staff and walk alone; some keep modest vows and reject wealth, content in low estate.

sentences.zh: 故漆園外楚，忌在龜犧；

translations.literal: Thus the man of Lacquer Garden went outside Chu, fearing the turtle in the sacred pen;
translations.idiomatic: Thus Zhuangzi of Lacquer Garden left Chu, fearing the turtle in the sacred pen;

sentences.zh: 商洛遐遯，畏此駟馬。

translations.literal: the men of Shang and Luo dwelt far in seclusion, dreading these four-horse teams.
translations.idiomatic: the lords of Shang and Luo dwelt far in seclusion, dreading a team of four horses.

sentences.zh: 平仲辭邑，殷鑒於崔、慶，張臨挹滿，灼戒乎桑、霍。

translations.literal: Ping Zhong declined his fief, taking Cui and Qing as bright mirrors; Zhang faced a brimming cup and drew a blazing warning from Sang and Huo.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Ying declined his fief, taking Cui and Qing as warning; Zhang drew from a brimming cup the blazing lesson of Sang and Huo.

sentences.zh: 若君子覽茲二塗，則賢鄙之分既明，全喪之實又顯。

translations.literal: If a gentleman surveys these two paths, then the distinction between worthy and base is already clear, and the reality of preservation and ruin is likewise manifest.
translations.idiomatic: If a gentleman weighs these two paths, the line between worthy and base is clear, and what brings preservation or ruin is plain.

sentences.zh: 非知之難，慎之惟難，慎也者，言行之樞管乎！

translations.literal: It is not that knowing is difficult—only caution is difficult. Caution is the pivot and hub of words and deeds!
translations.idiomatic: The difficulty is not in knowing but in being cautious; caution is the pivot of word and deed.

sentences.zh: 夫據圖揮刃，愚夫弗為，臨淵登峭，莫不惴慄。

translations.literal: To grasp a chart and wield a blade—fools will not do it; to face a abyss and climb a precipice—none do not tremble with fear.
translations.idiomatic: To hold a chart and wield a blade—fools will not do it; to stand by an abyss and climb a cliff—none fails to tremble.

sentences.zh: 何則？

translations.literal: Why?
translations.idiomatic: Why?

sentences.zh: 害交故慮篤，患切而懼深。

translations.literal: Because harm is imminent, thought is earnest; because peril is pressing, fear is deep.
translations.idiomatic: Because harm is near, thought runs deep; because peril presses close, fear runs deep.

sentences.zh: 故《詩》曰：「不敢暴虎，不敢馮河。

translations.literal: Thus the Odes say: "I dare not attack a tiger bare-handed, I dare not cross a river on foot."
translations.idiomatic: Thus the Odes say: "I dare not attack a tiger bare-handed; I dare not ford a river on foot."

sentences.zh: 」慎微之謂也。

translations.literal: This is what is meant by caution in small things.
translations.idiomatic: That is what is meant by caution in small things.

sentences.zh: 故庖子涉族，怵然為戒，差之一毫，弊猶如此。

translations.literal: Thus when Cook Ding crossed the clan archery ground, he was visibly wary and took it as a warning; if a discrepancy of one hair's breadth could bring such harm,
translations.idiomatic: When Cook Ding crossed the clan archery ground he was visibly wary and took warning—even a discrepancy of one hair's breadth could bring such harm;

sentences.zh: 況乎觸害犯機，自投死地。

translations.literal: how much more when one touches harm and violates the trigger, casting oneself into the ground of death!
translations.idiomatic: how much more when one courts harm and springs the trap, casting oneself into the ground of death!

sentences.zh: 禍福之具，內充外斥，陵九折於邛僰，泛衝波於呂梁，傾側成於俄頃，性命哀而莫救。

translations.literal: The instruments of fortune and calamity fill within and press without; one scales the nine bends of Qiong and Bo, floats the rushing waves of Lüliang—tilting and capsizing come in an instant, and life is mournful with no one to save it.
translations.idiomatic: Fortune and calamity fill within and press without; one scales the nine bends of Qiong and Bo, rides the rushing waves of Lüliang—capsizing comes in an instant, and life is lost with none to save it.

sentences.zh: 嗚呼！

translations.literal: Alas!
translations.idiomatic: Alas!

sentences.zh: 嗚呼！

translations.literal: Alas!
translations.idiomatic: Alas!

sentences.zh: 故語有之曰：誠能慎之，福之根也。

translations.literal: Thus a saying runs: "If one can truly be cautious, that is the root of fortune."
translations.idiomatic: A saying runs: "If one can truly be cautious, that is the root of fortune."

sentences.zh: 曰是何傷，禍之門爾。

translations.literal: "What harm is that?"—it is the gate of calamity.
translations.idiomatic: "What harm is that?"—it is the gate of calamity.

sentences.zh: 言慎而已矣。

translations.literal: The talk is of caution, nothing more.
translations.idiomatic: The message is caution—nothing more.

sentences.zh: 亮布衣儒生，僥倖際會，既居宰輔，兼總重權。

translations.literal: Liang was a common-cloth Confucian scholar who by chance met a timely opportunity; once he occupied the post of chief minister, he also held overall heavy authority.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Liang was a scholar in plain robes who met a timely opportunity; once he stood as chief minister, he held supreme authority as well.

sentences.zh: 少帝失德，內懷憂懼，作《感物賦》以寄意焉。

translations.literal: Emperor Shao lost virtue; within himself Liang harbored worry and fear, and composed the Rhapsody on Moved Things to lodge his intent.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Shao proved unworthy, Fu Liang was inwardly fearful and wrote the Rhapsody on Moved Things to express his feelings.

sentences.zh: 其辭曰：

translations.literal: Its text says:
translations.idiomatic: The rhapsody reads:

sentences.zh: 余以暮秋之月，述職內禁，夜清務隙，遊目藝苑。

translations.literal: I, in the month of late autumn, performed my duties within the forbidden precinct; when the night was clear and tasks had a gap, I let my gaze wander through the garden of arts.
translations.idiomatic: In the late-autumn month I discharged my duties within the palace precincts; when the night grew clear and my tasks had a pause, I let my gaze wander through the garden of letters.

sentences.zh: 於時風霜初戒，蟄類尚繁，飛蛾翔羽，翩翾滿室，赴軒幌，集明燭者，必以燋滅為度。

translations.literal: At that time the wind and frost had just begun their warning; hibernating creatures were still numerous; flying moths and soaring insects, fluttering and whirling, filled the chamber. Those that rushed to the window curtains and gathered at the bright candles invariably took scorching extinction as their measure.
translations.idiomatic: The wind and frost had just begun their warning; dormant creatures were still plentiful; moths and gnats fluttered through the room. Those that rushed to the curtains and gathered at the bright candles took their own burning as the measure of all things.

sentences.zh: 雖則微物，矜懷者久之。

translations.literal: Though they were slight creatures, one who cherishes feeling was long moved by them.
translations.idiomatic: Though they were tiny creatures, a man of feeling could not quickly put them from his mind.

sentences.zh: 退感莊生異鵲之事，與彼同迷而忘反鑒之道，此先師所以鄙智，及齊客所以難日論也。

translations.literal: Retiring, I was moved by Master Zhuang's tale of the strange magpie; like them I was equally deluded and forgot the way of turning back to reflect; this is why the former Master despised mere cleverness, and why the guest of Qi found the day-long disputation hard to sustain.
translations.idiomatic: Withdrawn in thought, I recalled Master Zhuang's tale of the strange magpie—how, like these insects, one may be equally deluded and forget the way of turning back to reflect; this is why the sages despised mere cleverness, and why the Qi disputant could not sustain his argument for a single day.

sentences.zh: 悵然有懷，感物興思，遂賦之云爾。

translations.literal: Sighing, I harbored feeling; moved by things, I raised thought—and so composed this rhapsody.
translations.idiomatic: Sighing, I took thought from what I had seen; moved by things, I gave my feelings voice—and so composed this rhapsody.

sentences.zh: 在西成之暮晷，肅皇命於禁中。

translations.literal: In the evening shadows of western accomplishment, I reverently bore the imperial charge within the forbidden palace.
translations.idiomatic: In the evening shadows of autumn's western quarter, I reverently bore the imperial charge within the palace.

sentences.zh: 聆蜻蛚於前廡，鑒朗月於房櫳。

translations.literal: I listened to crickets in the front corridor and beheld the bright moon through the lattice window.
translations.idiomatic: I listened to crickets in the front corridor and beheld the bright moon through the lattice window.

sentences.zh: 風蕭瑟以陵幌，霜皚皚而被墉。

translations.literal: The wind was bleak as it assailed the curtains; frost gleamed white as it covered the walls.
translations.idiomatic: Bleak wind assailed the curtains; gleaming frost whitened the walls.

sentences.zh: 憐鳴蜩之應節，惜落景之懷東。

translations.literal: I pitied the chirping cicada answering the season; I grieved the setting sun longing for the east.
translations.idiomatic: I pitied the chirping cicada answering the season; I grieved the setting sun that yearns toward the east.

sentences.zh: 嗟勞人之萃感，何夕永而慮充。

translations.literal: Alas for the toiling man gathering feelings—why does the long evening never end, while cares fill the heart!
translations.idiomatic: Alas for the toiling man who gathers up his feelings—why does the long night never end while cares crowd the heart!

sentences.zh: 眇今古以遐念，若循環之無終。

translations.literal: I gaze on present and past from afar; it is like a cycle without end.
translations.idiomatic: I gaze from afar on present and past, as on a cycle without end.

sentences.zh: 詠倚相之遺矩，希董生之方融。

translations.literal: I chant Yi Xiang's handed-down rule and hope for Master Dong's harmonious fusion.
translations.idiomatic: I chant Yi Xiang's handed-down rule and hope for Master Dong's harmonious fusion.

sentences.zh: 鑽光燈而散袠，溫聖哲之遺蹤。

translations.literal: I drill by lamplight and loosen my sash; I warm myself at the traces left by the sages.
translations.idiomatic: I study by lamplight and loosen my robe; I warm myself at the traces of the sages.

sentences.zh: 墳素杳以難暨，九流紛其異封。

translations.literal: The tomb classics and plain texts are remote and hard to reach; the Nine Schools dispute in separate branches.
translations.idiomatic: The ancient classics lie remote and hard to reach; the nine schools dispute in separate branches.

sentences.zh: 領三百於無邪，貫五千於有宗。

translations.literal: I take in the three hundred without heterodoxy and thread through the five thousand with a single master.
translations.idiomatic: I take in the three hundred odes without heterodoxy and thread through the five thousand words with a single master.

sentences.zh: 考舊聞於前史，訪心跡於汙隆。

translations.literal: I examine old reports in former histories and visit heart-traces in rise and fall.
translations.idiomatic: I examine old reports in the histories and trace men's hearts through rise and fall.

sentences.zh: 豈夷阻之在運，將全喪之由躬。

translations.literal: Is it that hardship and obstruction lie in fate—or that preservation and ruin depend on one's own person?
translations.idiomatic: Is hardship and obstruction ordained by fate—or do preservation and ruin depend on one's own person?

sentences.zh: 遊翰林之彪炳，嘉美手於良工。

translations.literal: I roam the resplendent forest of letters and praise the skilled hand of the fine craftsman.
translations.idiomatic: I roam the resplendent forest of letters and praise the skilled hand of the fine craftsman.

sentences.zh: 辭存麗而去穢，旨既雅而能通。

translations.literal: The wording keeps beauty and casts off filth; the purport is already refined yet can penetrate.
translations.idiomatic: The wording keeps its beauty and casts off filth; the purport is refined yet penetrates.

sentences.zh: 雖源流之深浩，且揚搉而發蒙。

translations.literal: Though the source-stream is deep and vast, for now I raise and weigh it, opening the unenlightened.
translations.idiomatic: Though the source-stream runs deep and vast, for now I raise and weigh it, opening the unenlightened.

sentences.zh: 習習飛蚋，飄飄纖蠅，緣幌求隙，望爓思陵。

translations.literal: Whirring, whirring—flying gnats; drifting, drifting—slender flies; they climb the curtain seeking a gap and gaze at the flame, thinking to ascend.
translations.idiomatic: Whirring gnats, drifting flies—they climb the curtain seeking a gap and gaze at the flame, thinking to soar.

sentences.zh: 糜蘭膏而無悔，赴朗燭而未懲。

translations.literal: They waste orchid balm without regret and rush to the bright candle without chastening.
translations.idiomatic: They waste orchid balm without regret and rush to the bright candle without heed.

sentences.zh: 瞻前軌之既覆，忘改轍於後乘。

translations.literal: They behold the track ahead already overturned yet forget to change their carriage's course behind.
translations.idiomatic: They see the track ahead already overturned yet forget to change course behind.

sentences.zh: 匪微物之足悼，悵永念而捬膺。

translations.literal: It is not that slight creatures are worth grieving; I sigh in long thought and beat my breast.
translations.idiomatic: It is not these slight creatures that are worth grieving; I sigh in long thought and beat my breast.

sentences.zh: 彼人道之為貴，參二儀而比靈。

translations.literal: That the human way is prized—joining the Two Standards and matching their spirit.
translations.idiomatic: That the human way is prized—joining heaven and earth and matching their spirit.

sentences.zh: 稟清曠以授氣，脩緣督而為經。

translations.literal: Receiving clear openness in the gift of breath, cultivating the spine's conduit as one's canon.
translations.idiomatic: Receiving clarity in the gift of breath, taking cultivation of the spine's conduit as one's canon.

sentences.zh: 照安危於心術，鏡纖兆於未形。

translations.literal: Illumining safety and peril in the art of the heart; mirroring fine omens before they take form.
translations.idiomatic: Illumining safety and peril in the art of the heart; mirroring fine omens before they take shape.

sentences.zh: 有徇末而舍本，或耽欲而忘生。

translations.literal: Some pursue the branch and abandon the root; some cling to desire and forget life.
translations.idiomatic: Some pursue the branch and abandon the root; some cling to desire and forget life.

sentences.zh: 碎隨侯於微爵，捐所重而要輕。

translations.literal: They smash the Marquis of Sui's gem for a petty rank and abandon what is weighty to grasp what is light.
translations.idiomatic: They smash the Marquis of Sui's pearl for a petty rank and abandon what is weighty to seize what is light.

sentences.zh: 矧昆蟲之所昧，在智士其猶嬰。

translations.literal: How much more are insects darkened; even in a wise man it is still like an infant.
translations.idiomatic: How much more are mere insects benighted; even the wise man remains as helpless as an infant.

sentences.zh: 悟雕陵於莊氏，幾鑒濁而迷清。

translations.literal: Awakening to Diao-ling through Master Zhuang, almost discerning the turbid yet mistaking the clear.
translations.idiomatic: Learning from Zhuangzi's tale of Diao-ling, I nearly discern the turbid—yet still mistake the clear.

sentences.zh: 仰前脩之懿軌，知吾跡之未并。

translations.literal: Looking up to former exemplars' fine tracks, I know my footsteps have not matched them.
translations.idiomatic: Looking up to the fine paths of former worthies, I know my own footsteps have not kept pace.

sentences.zh: 雖宋元之外占，曷在予之克明。

translations.literal: Though Song and Yuan had auguries surpassing others, how could they compare to my clarity?
translations.idiomatic: Though Song and Yuan had prognostications beyond the ordinary, how could they match what I might grasp?

sentences.zh: 豈知反之徒爾，喟投翰以增情。

translations.literal: Who knew turning back was merely thus; I sigh and cast down my brush to deepen feeling.
translations.idiomatic: Who knew that turning back would come to only this? I sigh and lay down my brush, and my grief grows the heavier.

sentences.zh: 初，奉迎大駕，道路賦詩三首，其一篇有悔懼之辭，曰：「夙櫂發皇邑，有人祖我舟。

translations.literal: At first, when welcoming the imperial carriage, on the road he composed three poems; one had words of remorse and fear, saying: "At dawn I ply oars departing the imperial city; someone sees me off at my boat."
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, while escorting the imperial carriage, he composed three poems on the journey. One contained words of remorse and dread, which read: "At dawn I ply my oars and leave the imperial city; someone has come to see my boat off."

sentences.zh: 餞離不以幣，贈言重琳球。

translations.literal: Farewell parting not with mere gifts; the words offered weigh like fine jade.
translations.idiomatic: The parting feast was not paid in mere gifts; the counsel given weighed like precious jade.

sentences.zh: 知止道攸貴，懷祿義所尤。

translations.literal: Knowing when to stop—the Way is thereby prized; clinging to emolument is what righteousness condemns.
translations.idiomatic: Knowing when to stop is what the Way holds dear; clinging to salary is what righteousness most condemns.

sentences.zh: 四牡倦長路，君轡可以收。

translations.literal: The four steeds weary on the long road; my lord's reins may now be drawn in.
translations.idiomatic: The four horses are weary from the long road; my lord may now gather in the reins.

sentences.zh: 張、邴結晨軌，疏、董頓夕輈。

translations.literal: Zhang and Bing tied their morning courses; Shu and Dong halted their evening chariots.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Chang and Bing Ji bound up their morning tracks; Shu Guang and Dong Zhongshu stilled their evening wheels.

sentences.zh: 東隅誠已謝，西景逝不留。

translations.literal: The eastern corner has truly faded; the western light departs and does not stay.
translations.idiomatic: The morning sun has truly set; the evening light passes and will not linger.

sentences.zh: 性命安可圖，懷此作前脩。

translations.literal: Life and fate—how can they be plotted? Holding this, I take former exemplars as my model.
translations.idiomatic: How can life and fate be schemed for? Holding this thought, I take the ancients as my guide.

sentences.zh: 敷衽銘篤誨，引帶佩嘉謀。

translations.literal: Spreading my robe, I inscribe earnest admonition; tying my sash, I wear worthy counsel.
translations.idiomatic: I spread my robe and inscribe earnest teaching; I fasten my sash and keep worthy counsel at my side.

sentences.zh: 迷寵非予志，厚德良未酬。

translations.literal: Bewitchment by favor is not my intent; deep kindness has indeed gone unrewarded.
translations.idiomatic: To be lost in favor was never my aim; great kindness, alas, I have not yet repaid.

sentences.zh: 撫躬愧疲朽，三省慙爵浮。

translations.literal: Touching my person, I blush at my wearied decay; thrice reflecting, I shame my rank's lightness.
translations.idiomatic: When I touch my own person I blush at my worn-out age; thrice reflecting, I am ashamed that my rank sits too high.

sentences.zh: 重明照蓬艾，萬品同率由。

translations.literal: The duplicate sun illumines mugwort and artemisia; ten thousand things alike follow its lead.
translations.idiomatic: The second sun shines even on mugwort and wormwood; the myriad creatures all follow where it leads.

sentences.zh: 忠誥豈假知，式微發直謳。

translations.literal: Loyal admonition needs no borrowed wisdom; in decline I raise a straight song.
translations.idiomatic: Loyal remonstrance needs no borrowed wit; in my decline I lift a plain, honest song.

sentences.zh: 」亮自知傾覆，求退無由，又作辛有、穆生、董仲道贊，稱其見微之美。

translations.literal: " Liang knew himself doomed to ruin and could find no way to retire; he also composed encomia to Xin You, Mu Sheng, and Dong Zhongdao, praising their beauty of perceiving subtle signs.
translations.idiomatic: " Fu Liang knew his fall was near and could find no way to withdraw. He also wrote encomia to Xin You, Mu Sheng, and Dong Zhongdao, praising their gift for discerning trouble while it was still slight.

sentences.zh: 長子演，秘書郎，先亮卒。

translations.literal: His eldest son Yan was a secretary gentleman and died before Liang.
translations.idiomatic: His eldest son Yan, a secretary gentleman, died before Fu Liang.

sentences.zh: 演弟悝、湛逃亡。

translations.literal: Yan's younger brothers Hui and Zhan fled into hiding.
translations.idiomatic: Yan's younger brothers Hui and Zhan went into flight.

sentences.zh: 湛弟都，徙建安郡；

translations.literal: Zhan's younger brother Du was banished to Jian'an commandery;
translations.idiomatic: Zhan's younger brother Du was exiled to Jian'an commandery;

sentences.zh: 世祖孝建之中，並還京師。

translations.literal: in the Xiaojian era of Emperor Xiaowu, all were returned to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: during the Xiaojian reign of Emperor Xiaowu, all were permitted to return to the capital.

sentences.zh: 檀道濟，高平金鄉人，左將軍韶少弟也。

translations.literal: Tan Daoji was a man of Jinxian in Gaoping, the youngest brother of Left General Shao.
translations.idiomatic: Tan Daoji was a native of Jinxian in Gaoping and the youngest brother of Left General Tan Shao.

sentences.zh: 少孤，居喪備禮。

translations.literal: Orphaned young, in mourning he observed every rite.
translations.idiomatic: Orphaned in youth, he observed every detail of the mourning rites.

sentences.zh: 奉姊事兄，以和謹致稱。

translations.literal: Serving his elder sister and honoring his elder brother, he won praise for harmony and prudence.
translations.idiomatic: He cared for his elder sister and served his elder brother, and was praised for his gentle, careful conduct.

sentences.zh: 高祖創義，道濟從入京城，參高祖建武軍事，轉征西。

translations.literal: When Gaozu Liu Yu raised the righteous cause, Daoji followed him into the capital, served on Gaozu's Jianwu staff, and was transferred to the western campaign staff.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu Liu Yu raised the banner of righteousness, Daoji followed him into the capital, served on Gaozu's Jianwu military staff, and was later transferred to the western campaign staff.

sentences.zh: 討平魯山，禽桓振，除輔國參軍、南陽太守。

translations.literal: He pacified Lushan, captured Huan Zhen, and was appointed aide to the state-supporting army and governor of Nanyang.
translations.idiomatic: He helped pacify Lushan, captured Huan Zhen, and was appointed aide to the state-supporting army and governor of Nanyang.

sentences.zh: 以建義勳，封吳興縣五等侯。

translations.literal: For merit in founding the righteous cause, he was enfeoffed as fifth-rank Marquis of Wuxing county.
translations.idiomatic: For his merit in the founding campaign, he was enfeoffed as fifth-rank Marquis of Wuxing county.

sentences.zh: 盧循寇逆，群盜互起，郭寄生等聚作唐，以道濟為揚武將軍、天門太守討平之。

translations.literal: When Lu Xun rebelled and bandits rose everywhere, Guo Jisheng and others gathered at Zuotang; Daoji was made General Who Displays Might and governor of Tianmen to suppress them.
translations.idiomatic: When Lu Xun rose in rebellion and bandits sprang up on every side, Guo Jisheng and others gathered at Zuotang. Daoji was appointed General Who Displays Might and governor of Tianmen to put them down.

sentences.zh: 又從劉道規討桓謙、荀林等，率厲文武，身先士卒，所向摧破。

translations.literal: He also followed Liu Daogui in campaigning against Huan Qian, Xun Lin, and others, rousing civil and military officers, taking the lead before the ranks, and crushing all he faced.
translations.idiomatic: He also followed Liu Daogui against Huan Qian, Xun Lin, and others, inspiring both civil and military officers, charging ahead of his men, and breaking every foe in his path.

sentences.zh: 及徐道覆來逼，道規親出拒戰，道濟戰功居多。

translations.literal: When Xu Daofu pressed close, Daogui went out in person to resist; Daoji's battle merit was the greater part.
translations.idiomatic: When Xu Daofu pressed the attack, Daogui went out in person to meet him, and the greater share of the victory belonged to Daoji.

sentences.zh: 遷安遠護軍、武陵內史。

translations.literal: He was transferred to protector of Anyuan and interior minister of Wuling.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to protector of Anyuan and interior minister of Wuling.

sentences.zh: 復為太尉參軍，拜中書侍郎，轉寧朔將軍，參太尉軍事。

translations.literal: He again served as aide to the Grand Commander, was appointed vice director of the Secretariat, transferred to General Who Pacifies the North, and joined the Grand Commander's staff.
translations.idiomatic: He again served as aide to the Grand Commander, was appointed vice director of the Secretariat, promoted to General Who Pacifies the North, and joined the Grand Commander's military staff.

sentences.zh: 以前後功封作唐縣男，食邑四百戶。

translations.literal: For his successive merits he was enfeoffed as Baron of Zuotang county with a fief of four hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: For his repeated victories he was enfeoffed as Baron of Zuotang county with a fief of four hundred households.

sentences.zh: 補太尉主簿、諮議參軍。

translations.literal: He was appointed chief clerk to the Grand Commander and consulting staff officer.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed chief clerk to the Grand Commander and consulting staff officer.

sentences.zh: 豫章公世子為征虜將軍，鎮京口，道濟為司馬、臨淮太守。

translations.literal: When the heir of the Duke of Yuzhang served as General Who Punishes the Barbarians and garrisoned Jingkou, Daoji was his marshal and governor of Linhuai.
translations.idiomatic: When the heir of the Duke of Yuzhang served as General Who Punishes the Barbarians and held Jingkou, Daoji was his marshal and governor of Linhuai.

sentences.zh: 又為世子西中郎司馬、梁國內史。

translations.literal: He also served as western bureau marshal to the heir and interior minister of Liang.
translations.idiomatic: He also served as western bureau marshal to the heir and interior minister of Liang.

sentences.zh: 復為世子征虜將軍司馬，加冠軍將軍。

translations.literal: He again became marshal to the heir as General Who Punishes the Barbarians and was given the additional title of General Who Vanquishes the Foe.
translations.idiomatic: He again became marshal on the heir's staff as General Who Punishes the Barbarians and was given the additional title of General Who Vanquishes the Foe.

sentences.zh: 義熙十二年，高祖北伐，以道濟為前鋒出淮、肥，所至諸城戍望風降服。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year of Yixi, Gaozu's northern campaign made Daoji vanguard through the Huai and Fei region; every walled post he reached surrendered at the sight of his banners.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year of Yixi (416), during Gaozu's northern expedition, Daoji led the vanguard through the Huai and Fei region, and every fortress and garrison he approached surrendered at once.

sentences.zh: 進克許昌，獲偽寧朔將軍、潁川太守姚坦及大將楊業。

translations.literal: Advancing he took Xuchang and captured the false-state General Who Pacifies the North and governor of Yingchuan Yao Tan, together with the great commander Yang Ye.
translations.idiomatic: Pressing forward, he took Xuchang and captured the Northern Wei general Yao Tan, who held the titles General Who Pacifies the North and governor of Yingchuan, along with the great commander Yang Ye.

sentences.zh: 至成臯，偽兗州刺史韋華降。

translations.literal: Reaching Chenggao, the false-state inspector of Yan Province Wei Hua surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: At Chenggao, the Northern Wei inspector of Yan Province, Wei Hua, surrendered.

sentences.zh: 逕進洛陽，偽平南將軍陳留公姚沈歸順。

translations.literal: He pressed straight on to Luoyang; the false-state General Who Pacifies the South, Duke of Chenliu Yao Shen, submitted.
translations.idiomatic: He marched straight on to Luoyang, where the Northern Wei General Who Pacifies the South, Duke of Chenliu Yao Shen, came over to his side.

sentences.zh: 凡拔城破壘，俘四千餘人。

translations.literal: In all, in storming cities and breaking ramparts, he took more than four thousand prisoners.
translations.idiomatic: In all, in storming cities and breaking fortifications, he took more than four thousand prisoners.

sentences.zh: 議者謂應悉戮以為京觀。

translations.literal: Counselors said they should all be slaughtered to make a victory mound.
translations.idiomatic: Some at court argued that the prisoners should all be slaughtered to build a victory mound.

sentences.zh: 道濟曰：「伐罪弔民，正在今日。

translations.literal: Daoji said: "To punish the guilty and comfort the people—this is exactly the day for it."
translations.idiomatic: Daoji said, "To punish the guilty and comfort the people—that is what today is for."

sentences.zh: 」皆釋而遣之。

translations.literal: " All were released and sent away.
translations.idiomatic: " He released them all and sent them home.

sentences.zh: 於是戎夷感悅，相率歸之者甚眾。

translations.literal: Thereupon the tribes were moved and delighted, and very many came over in succession.
translations.idiomatic: The frontier peoples were deeply moved, and a great host came over to submit in succession.

sentences.zh: 進據潼關，與諸軍共破姚紹。

translations.literal: Advancing he held Tong Pass and, with the other armies, defeated Yao Shao.
translations.idiomatic: He advanced and seized Tong Pass, and together with the other armies defeated Yao Shao.

sentences.zh: 長安既平，以為征虜將軍、琅邪內史。

translations.literal: Once Chang'an was pacified, he was made General Who Punishes the Barbarians and interior minister of Langye.
translations.idiomatic: After Chang'an was pacified, he was appointed General Who Punishes the Barbarians and interior minister of Langye.

sentences.zh: 世子當鎮江陵，復以道濟為西中郎司馬、持節、南蠻校尉。

translations.literal: When the heir was to garrison Jiangling, Daoji was again made western bureau marshal, bearer of the staff, and colonel of the southern barbarians.
translations.idiomatic: When the heir was posted to Jiangling, Daoji was again made western bureau marshal, bearer of the staff, and colonel of the southern barbarians.

sentences.zh: 又加征虜將軍。

translations.literal: He was further given the title General Who Punishes the Barbarians.
translations.idiomatic: He was further promoted to General Who Punishes the Barbarians.

sentences.zh: 遷宋國侍中，領世子中庶子，兗州大中正。

translations.literal: He was transferred to palace attendant of the Song state, concurrent supervisor of the heir's household, and chief rectifier of Yan Province.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to palace attendant of the Song state, made concurrent supervisor of the heir's household, and appointed chief rectifier of Yan Province.

sentences.zh: 高祖受命，轉護軍，加散騎常侍，領石頭戍事。

translations.literal: When Gaozu received the Mandate, Daoji was transferred to general who guards the army, given the additional title of regular attendant of the scattered cavalry, and put in charge of the Shitou garrison.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu received the Mandate, Daoji was made general who guards the army, given the additional title of regular attendant of the scattered cavalry, and put in charge of the Shitou garrison.

sentences.zh: 聽直入殿省。

translations.literal: He was permitted to enter the palace offices directly.
translations.idiomatic: He was permitted to enter the palace offices without prior announcement.

sentences.zh: 以佐命功，改封永脩縣公，食邑二千戶。

translations.literal: For merit in assisting the Mandate, his fief was changed to Duke of Yongxiu county with two thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: For his merit in helping Gaozu win the throne, his title was changed to Duke of Yongxiu county with a fief of two thousand households.

sentences.zh: 徙為丹陽尹，護軍如故。

translations.literal: He was moved to governor of Danyang while remaining general who guards the army as before.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to governor of Danyang while retaining his post as general who guards the army.

sentences.zh: 高祖不豫，給班劍二十人。

translations.literal: When Gaozu fell ill, he was granted twenty armed attendants with ceremonial swords.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu fell gravely ill, he was granted an escort of twenty armed attendants bearing ceremonial swords.

sentences.zh: 出監南徐、兗之江北、淮南諸郡軍事、鎮北將軍、南兗州刺史。

translations.literal: He went out to oversee military affairs in the southern Xu, northern Jiang region of Yan, and Huainan commanderies, as General Who Pacifies the North and inspector of Southern Yan Province.
translations.idiomatic: He went out to oversee military affairs in southern Xu, the northern Jiang districts of Yan, and the Huainan commanderies, serving as General Who Pacifies the North and inspector of Southern Yan Province.

sentences.zh: 景平元年，虜圍青州刺史竺夔於東陽城，夔告急。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jingping, the barbarians besieged Qing Province inspector Zhu Kui at Dongyang city, and Kui sent an urgent appeal.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Jingping (423), the Northern Wei barbarians besieged Qing Province inspector Zhu Kui at Dongyang city, and Kui sent an urgent appeal for help.

sentences.zh: 加道濟使持節、監征討諸軍事，與王仲德救東陽。

translations.literal: Daoji was given the staff of envoy, oversight of all punitive forces, and joined Wang Zhongde in relieving Dongyang.
translations.idiomatic: Daoji was given the staff of envoy and overall command of the punitive armies, and marched with Wang Zhongde to relieve Dongyang.

sentences.zh: 未及至，虜燒營，焚攻具遁走。

translations.literal: Before they arrived, the barbarians burned their camp, set fire to their siege engines, and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Before they arrived, the barbarians burned their camp, destroyed their siege equipment, and fled.

sentences.zh: 將追之，城內無食，乃開窖取久穀；

translations.literal: About to pursue them, the city had no food, so they opened the granary pits to take out long-stored grain;
translations.idiomatic: They were about to pursue when they found the city had no food, so they opened the underground granaries to bring out grain stored long before;

sentences.zh: 窖深數丈，出穀作米，已經再宿；

translations.literal: the pits were several zhang deep; bringing out the grain and milling it took two full nights;
translations.idiomatic: the pits were several zhang deep, and hauling out the grain and milling it took two full nights;

sentences.zh: 虜去已遠，不復可追，乃止。

translations.literal: the barbarians were already far away and could no longer be pursued, so they stopped.
translations.idiomatic: by then the barbarians were too far away to overtake, and the pursuit was abandoned.

sentences.zh: 還鎮廣陵。

translations.literal: He returned to garrison Guangling.
translations.idiomatic: He then returned to his post at Guangling.

sentences.zh: 及討謝晦，道濟率軍繼到彥之。

translations.literal: When campaigning against Xie Hui, Daoji led his army to follow up on Yan Zhi.
translations.idiomatic: During the campaign against Xie Hui, Daoji led his army to reinforce Yan Zhi.

sentences.zh: 彥之戰敗，退保隱圻，會道濟至。

translations.literal: Yan Zhi was defeated and withdrew to hold Yinfan; just then Daoji arrived.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Zhi had been defeated and withdrew to hold Yinfan when Daoji arrived.

sentences.zh: 晦本謂道濟與羨之等同誅，忽聞來上，人情凶懼，遂不戰自潰。

translations.literal: Hui had thought Daoji would be executed together with Xianzhi and the others; suddenly hearing he had come upstream, men's hearts turned fearful, and without fighting they scattered of themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Hui had assumed Daoji would be executed along with Xu Xianzhi and the others. When word suddenly came that Daoji was marching upstream, panic spread through his ranks, and his army collapsed without a fight.

sentences.zh: 事平，遷都督江州之江夏、豫州之西陽、新蔡、晉熙四郡諸軍事、征南大將軍、開府儀同三司、江州刺史，持節、常侍如故；

translations.literal: When the affair was settled, he was transferred to overall command of military affairs in the four commanderies of Jiangxia in Jiang Province, Xiyang, Xincai, and Jinxi in Yu Province, made Grand General Who Campaigns South, given the privilege of an office equal to the Three Excellencies, and made inspector of Jiang Province, with the staff and regular attendant as before;
translations.idiomatic: After the rebellion was crushed, he was made commander of military affairs in Jiangxia of Jiang Province and Xiyang, Xincai, and Jinxi of Yu Province, promoted to Grand General Who Campaigns South with an office equal to the Three Excellencies, and appointed inspector of Jiang Province, retaining his staff and post as regular attendant;

sentences.zh: 增封千戶。

translations.literal: his fief was increased by one thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: and his fief was increased by one thousand households.

sentences.zh: 元嘉八年，到彥之伐索虜，已平河南，尋復失之；

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Yuanjia, Yan Zhi campaigned against the Northern Wei barbarians, had already pacified the region south of the Yellow River, but soon lost it again;
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year of Yuanjia (431), Yan Zhi campaigned against the Northern Wei barbarians and had pacified the region south of the Yellow River, only to lose it again soon after;

sentences.zh: 金墉、虎牢並沒，虜逼滑臺。

translations.literal: Jinyong and Hulao both fell, and the barbarians pressed Huatai.
translations.idiomatic: Jinyong and Hulao both fell, and the barbarians pressed Huatai.

sentences.zh: 加道濟都督征討諸軍事，率眾北討。

translations.literal: Daoji was given overall command of the punitive armies and led the host north to campaign.
translations.idiomatic: Daoji was given overall command of the punitive armies and led a great force north.

sentences.zh: 軍至東平壽張縣，值虜安平公乙旃眷。

translations.literal: The army reached Shouzhang county in Dongping and encountered the barbarian Prince of Peace Yizhan Juan.
translations.idiomatic: The army reached Shouzhang in Dongping, where it encountered the Northern Wei Prince of Peace, Yizhan Juan.

sentences.zh: 道濟率寧朔將軍王仲德、驍騎將軍段宏奮擊，大破之。

translations.literal: Daoji led General Who Pacifies the North Wang Zhongde and General of Valiant Cavalry Duan Hong in a fierce assault and routed them utterly.
translations.idiomatic: Daoji led Wang Zhongde, General Who Pacifies the North, and Duan Hong, General of Valiant Cavalry, in a fierce assault and won a crushing victory.

sentences.zh: 轉戰至高梁亭，虜寧南將軍、濟州刺史壽昌公悉頰庫結前後邀戰，道濟分遣段宏及臺隊主沈虔之等奇兵擊之，即斬悉頰庫結。

translations.literal: Fighting on to Gaoliang Pavilion, the barbarian General Who Pacifies the South, inspector of Ji Province, Duke of Shouchang Xibaku Jie blocked him front and rear; Daoji detached Duan Hong and the capital detachment commander Shen Qianzhi and others with surprise forces to strike, and at once beheaded Xibaku Jie.
translations.idiomatic: Pressing the fight to Gaoliang Pavilion, the Northern Wei General Who Pacifies the South and inspector of Ji Province, Duke of Shouchang Xibaku Jie, intercepted him from front and rear. Daoji sent Duan Hong and the capital detachment commander Shen Qianzhi with flanking troops, and Xibaku Jie was beheaded on the spot.

sentences.zh: 道濟進至濟上，連戰二十餘日，前後數十交，虜眾盛，遂陷滑臺。

translations.literal: Daoji advanced to the Ji River region and fought for more than twenty days straight, clashing several dozen times; the barbarian host was strong, and Huatai finally fell.
translations.idiomatic: Daoji advanced to the Ji River and fought for more than twenty days, clashing several dozen times. The barbarian forces were too strong, and Huatai finally fell.

sentences.zh: 道濟於歷城全軍而反。

translations.literal: Daoji withdrew from Licheng with his army intact.
translations.idiomatic: Daoji withdrew from Licheng with his army intact.

sentences.zh: 進位司空，持節、常侍、都督、刺史並如故。

translations.literal: He was advanced to Minister of Works; bearer of the staff, regular attendant, commander, and inspector all remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Minister of Works, while his staff, post as regular attendant, command, and provincial inspectorate all remained unchanged.

sentences.zh: 還鎮尋陽。

translations.literal: He returned to garrison Xunyang.
translations.idiomatic: He returned to his post at Xunyang.

sentences.zh: 道濟立功前朝，威名甚重；

translations.literal: Daoji had won merit under the previous reign and his martial renown was very great;
translations.idiomatic: Daoji had won his laurels under the previous reign, and his martial renown was immense;

sentences.zh: 左右腹心，並經百戰，諸子又有才氣，朝廷疑畏之。

translations.literal: the men at his side and in his inner circle had all fought a hundred battles, and his sons were likewise talented and forceful—the court both suspected and feared him.
translations.idiomatic: the men at his side had all fought through a hundred battles, and his sons were talented and forceful as well. The court both suspected and feared him.

sentences.zh: 太祖寢疾累年，屢經危殆，彭城王義康慮宮車晏駕，道濟不可復制。

translations.literal: Taizu Emperor Wen had lain ill for years and repeatedly reached mortal peril; the Prince of Pengcheng Yikang feared that when the imperial carriage halted at dusk, Daoji could no longer be controlled.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu Emperor Wen had lain gravely ill for years and repeatedly hovered near death. The Prince of Pengcheng Yikang feared that when the emperor died, Tan Daoji would no longer be controllable.

sentences.zh: 十二年，上疾篤，會索虜為邊寇，召道濟入朝。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year the emperor's illness was grave; just then the Northern Wei barbarians raided the border, and Daoji was summoned to court.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year (435) the emperor's illness grew grave. Just then the Northern Wei barbarians raided the frontier, and Daoji was summoned to court.

sentences.zh: 既至，上間。

translations.literal: Once he arrived, the emperor had a respite.
translations.idiomatic: Once he arrived, the emperor's condition briefly improved.

sentences.zh: 十三年春，將遣道濟還鎮，已下船矣，會上疾動，召入祖道，收付廷尉。

translations.literal: In spring of the thirteenth year, about to send Daoji back to his post, he had already boarded the boat when the emperor's illness suddenly worsened; summoned back from the farewell feast, he was handed over to the Court of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the thirteenth year (436), the court was about to send Daoji back to his post. He had already boarded his boat when the emperor's illness suddenly worsened. Summoned back from his farewell feast, he was handed over to the Court of Justice.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「檀道濟階緣時幸，荷恩在昔，寵靈優渥，莫與為比。

translations.literal: The edict said: "Tan Daoji climbed by the fortune of the times, bore favor in days past, and received grace and honor beyond compare."
translations.idiomatic: The edict read: "Tan Daoji rose by the fortune of the times, received favor in days past, and was showered with grace and honor beyond compare."

sentences.zh: 曾不感佩殊遇，思答萬分，乃空懷疑貳，履霜日久。

translations.literal: " He never felt gratitude for this special treatment or thought to repay it in the slightest; instead he harbored disloyalty in vain, treading on frost for many a day."
translations.idiomatic: "He never felt gratitude for this extraordinary treatment or thought to repay it in the slightest. Instead he harbored disloyalty in his heart, and has long been walking on frost."

sentences.zh: 元嘉以來，猜阻滋結，不義不昵之心，附下罔上之事，固已暴之民聽，彰於遐邇。

translations.literal: " Since Yuanjia, suspicion and obstruction have steadily thickened; a heart neither righteous nor intimate, deeds of winning the lower ranks and deceiving superiors—these have already been exposed to public hearing and made plain far and near."
translations.idiomatic: "Since the Yuanjia era suspicion has only deepened. His heart has been neither loyal nor dutiful, and his habit of courting subordinates while deceiving his superiors is already known to the people and plain to all the realm."

sentences.zh: 謝靈運志凶辭醜，不臣顯著，納受邪說，每相容隱。

translations.literal: " Xie Lingyun's intent was vicious and his words ugly; his disloyalty was conspicuous, yet Daoji accepted his wicked counsel and repeatedly shielded him."
translations.idiomatic: "Xie Lingyun's intent was vicious and his words seditious; his disloyalty was plain for all to see, yet Daoji accepted his wicked counsel and repeatedly shielded him."

sentences.zh: 又潛散金貨，招誘剽猾，逋逃必至，實繁彌廣，日夜伺隙，希冀非望。

translations.literal: " He also secretly scattered gold and goods, recruiting violent ruffians; fugitives were sure to come, and their numbers grew ever broader, watching day and night for an opening and cherishing unlawful hopes."
translations.idiomatic: "He also secretly distributed gold and goods, recruiting violent ruffians. Fugitives flocked to him in ever greater numbers, and day and night he watched for an opening, nursing ambitions he had no right to hold."

sentences.zh: 鎮軍將軍仲德往年入朝，屢陳此跡。

translations.literal: " General of the Pacification Army Zhongde, on entering court in former years, repeatedly reported these traces."
translations.idiomatic: "General of the Pacification Army Wang Zhongde, when he came to court in earlier years, repeatedly reported these signs."

sentences.zh: 朕以其位居台鉉，豫班河岳，彌縫容養，庶或能革。

translations.literal: " We, because he stood among the highest pillars and shared in the ordering of the realm, patched and indulged him, hoping he might reform."
translations.idiomatic: "Because he stood among the highest ministers of state and shared in the governance of the realm, We patched things over and indulged him, hoping he might reform."

sentences.zh: 而長惡不悛，凶慝遂遘，因朕寢疾，規肆禍心。

translations.literal: " Yet he clung to evil and would not repent; his vicious intent then met its hour, and taking advantage of Our illness he plotted to unleash calamity."
translations.idiomatic: "Yet he clung to evil and would not repent. His vicious intent has now found its hour, and taking advantage of Our illness he plotted to unleash disaster."

sentences.zh: 前南蠻行參軍龐延祖具悉奸狀，密以啟聞。

translations.literal: " The former acting aide of the southern barbarians colonel, Pang Yanzu, knew the whole treacherous affair in detail and secretly reported it to Us."
translations.idiomatic: "The former acting aide on the southern barbarians staff, Pang Yanzu, knew the whole treacherous affair in detail and secretly reported it to Us."

sentences.zh: 夫君親無將，刑茲罔赦。

translations.literal: " For between ruler and father there is no 'general'—punish this and there is no pardon."
translations.idiomatic: "Between ruler and subject there can be no 'general' who stands above the law—when guilt is proved, there can be no pardon."

sentences.zh: 況罪釁深重，若斯之甚。

translations.literal: " How much more when the crime and guilt are as deep and grave as this."
translations.idiomatic: "How much more when the crime is as grave as this."

sentences.zh: 便可收付廷尉，肅正刑書。

translations.literal: " Let him at once be handed to the Court of Justice and the penal code duly enforced."
translations.idiomatic: "Let him at once be handed over to the Court of Justice and the penal code duly enforced."

sentences.zh: 事止元惡，餘無所問。

translations.literal: " The affair stops with the chief villain; beyond that, nothing further is to be investigated."
translations.idiomatic: "The affair stops with the chief culprit; beyond that, no further inquiry shall be made."

sentences.zh: 」於是收道濟及其子給事黃門侍郎植、司徒從事中郎粲、太子舍人隰、征北主簿承伯、秘書郎遵等八人，並於廷尉伏誅。

translations.literal: " Thereupon Daoji was arrested together with his sons—Gentleman at the Yellow Gate Zhi, aide to the Minister of Education Can, heir apparent household attendant Xi, chief clerk to the northern campaign Chengbo, secretary gentleman Zun, and two others, eight men in all—and all were executed at the Court of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: " Thereupon Daoji was arrested together with his sons Zhi, Can, Xi, Chengbo, and Zun and two others—eight men in all—and all were executed at the Court of Justice.

sentences.zh: 又收司空參軍薛彤，付建康伏法。

translations.literal: Xue Tong, staff officer of the Minister of Works, was also arrested and handed over to Jiankang for execution.
translations.idiomatic: Xue Tong, a staff officer of the minister of works, was also arrested and executed at Jiankang.

sentences.zh: 又遣尚書庫部郎顧仲文、建武將軍茅亨至尋陽，收道濟子夷、邕、演及司空參軍高進之，誅之。

translations.literal: Director of the Stores Section Gu Zhongwen and General Who Establishes Might Mao Heng were also dispatched to Xunyang to seize Daoji's sons Yi, Yong, and Yan and staff officer of the Minister of Works Gao Jinzhi, and execute them.
translations.idiomatic: The court also dispatched Gu Zhongwen, director of the stores section in the Secretariat, and General Who Establishes Might Mao Heng to Xunyang to seize Daoji's sons Yi, Yong, and Yan, along with his staff officer Gao Jinzhi, and put them to death.

sentences.zh: 薛彤、進之並道濟腹心，有勇力，時以比張飛、關羽。

translations.literal: Xue Tong and Jinzhi were both Daoji's inner confidants, brave and strong; at the time they were compared to Zhang Fei and Guan Yu.
translations.idiomatic: Xue Tong and Gao Jinzhi were both among Daoji's closest confidants, renowned for their courage and strength; contemporaries compared them to Zhang Fei and Guan Yu.

sentences.zh: 初，道濟見收，脫幘投地曰：「乃復壞汝萬里之長城！

translations.literal: When Daoji was first arrested, he pulled off his headcloth and cast it to the ground, saying: "You are once again destroying your ten-thousand-li Great Wall!
translations.idiomatic: When Daoji was first arrested, he pulled off his headcloth and flung it to the ground, crying: "You are destroying your own ten-thousand-li Great Wall!

sentences.zh: 」邕子孺乃被宥，世祖世，為奉朝請。

translations.literal: " Yong's son Ru was then pardoned; in the reign of Shizu he served as attendant at court audiences.
translations.idiomatic: " Yong's son Ru alone was pardoned; under Emperor Xiaowu he served as an attendant at court audiences.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：夫彈冠出里，結組登朝，道申於夷路，運艱於險轍，是以古人裴回於出處，交戰乎臨岐。

translations.literal: The historiographer says: Adjusting one's cap and leaving the lane, tying one's ribbons and ascending court—the Way is expressed on level roads, fortune turns hard on perilous tracks; therefore the ancients hesitated at going out or staying in and battled within themselves at the parting of ways.
translations.idiomatic: The historiographer remarks: When a man adjusts his cap and leaves his lane, ties his official ribbons and ascends to court, the Way may be realized on a level road yet fortune may turn harsh on a perilous track. That is why the ancients hesitated between withdrawal and service, warring within themselves at the crossroads.

sentences.zh: 若其任重於身，恩結自主，雖復據鼎承劍，悠然不以存歿為懷。

translations.literal: If one bears heavy responsibility upon one's person and favor is bound to one's lord, then even holding the tripod and receiving the sword, one is at ease and does not take survival or death to heart.
translations.idiomatic: When a man bears heavy responsibility upon his shoulders and his sovereign's favor is bound to his person, then even while holding the tripod and receiving the sword of authority, he remains at ease and does not make survival or death his chief concern.

sentences.zh: 當二公受言西殿，跪承顧託，若使死而可再，固以赴蹈為期也。

translations.literal: When the two lords received their charge in the Western Hall and knelt to receive the entrusted mandate, if death could come twice, they would surely have made rushing into danger their appointed term.
translations.idiomatic: When the two lords received their charge in the Western Hall and knelt to accept the dying emperor's entrusted mandate, had death been repeatable, they would surely have made hurling themselves into peril their appointed duty.

sentences.zh: 及逢權定之機，當震主之地，甫欲攘抑後禍，禦蔽身災，使桐宮有卒迫之痛，淮王非中霧之疾。

translations.literal: But when they met the moment of settled power and stood in the place that awed their lord, they only wished to push back later calamity and ward off personal disaster—so that the Tong Palace had the pain of sudden compulsion, and the Prince of Huai suffered not illness from mist within.
translations.idiomatic: But when they met the moment of settled authority and stood in positions that awed their sovereign, they sought only to ward off future calamity and shield themselves from disaster—so that the Tong Palace knew the anguish of sudden compulsion, and the Prince of Huai died not of an illness arising from within.

sentences.zh: 若以社稷為存亡，則義異於此。

translations.literal: If one takes the altars of state as the measure of survival or extinction, then righteousness differs from this.
translations.idiomatic: If one takes the altars of state as the measure of survival or extinction, then righteousness demands something different altogether.

sentences.zh: 但彭城無燕剌之釁，而有楚英之戮。

translations.literal: Yet Pengcheng had not the offense of Yan the Assassin, yet suffered the slaughter of Chu the Hero.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Prince of Pengcheng had committed no offense like that of Prince Dan of Yan, yet suffered a slaughter like that of Xiang Yu of Chu.

sentences.zh: 若使一昆延曆，亦未知定終所在也。

translations.literal: If one of the brothers had prolonged his reign, it is still unknown where the final end would have lain.
translations.idiomatic: If one of the brothers had been allowed to reign on, it is impossible to know where the final outcome would have fallen.

sentences.zh: 謝晦言不以賊遺君父，豈徒言哉！

translations.literal: Xie Hui's saying that one should not leave traitors to one's lord and father—was it mere words!
translations.idiomatic: Xie Hui's declaration that one must not leave traitors for one's lord and father to deal with—was that mere empty talk!
